verified.note: black lava flows and caldera on tan plain

features.name: Kolleru Lake
features.description: A large freshwater lake that has been almost entirely carved into a dense mosaic of rectangular fish and shrimp ponds, between the Godavari and Krishna deltas. It is one of the most striking aquaculture landscapes on Earth.
features.look_for: Huge mosaic of rectangular ponds

verified.note: pond mosaic clear at z12; reads as a mottled patch at z10

features.name: Juneau Icefield
features.description: The fifth largest ice field in the Western Hemisphere, straddling the Alaska-BC border and feeding Mendenhall, Taku and dozens of other glaciers. It has been monitored by a summer research program since 1946.
features.look_for: Huge ice plateau with radiating valley glaciers above fjords

features.name: Canyonlands
features.description: The Green and Colorado rivers join in deep entrenched meanders, dividing the land into the Island in the Sky, the Needles and the Maze, all visible as stacked red and white terraces.
features.look_for: Two meandering canyons joining among stepped red benches

verified.note: red canyon country; recentered on the confluence

features.name: Humboldt Glacier
features.description: Greenland's widest glacier front: about 100 km of ice cliff facing Kane Basin. Its front looks like a long ragged seam between ice sheet and sea ice.
features.look_for: Very long straight ice front along Kane Basin

features.name: Peace–Athabasca Delta
features.description: One of the largest freshwater inland deltas in the world, where the Peace and Athabasca rivers meet; its water level depends on ice jams and was altered by the W.A.C. Bennett Dam.
features.look_for: Mottled green delta of channels and shallow lakes at the west end of Lake Athabasca

features.name: Tufi fjords (Cape Nelson)
features.description: A volcanic peninsula whose radial valleys have been drowned into steep tropical rias known as the Tufi fjords. From above, forested ridges radiate from three volcanic peaks.
features.look_for: Radial ridges and drowned valleys on a coast

features.name: Astrolabe Reef & Kadavu
features.description: A barrier reef looping north from the long, ragged island of Kadavu in southern Fiji, outlining a turquoise lagoon with small islands. Dumont d'Urville's ship Astrolabe nearly sank on it in 1827.
features.look_for: Reef loop extending from a long island

features.name: Chuuk Lagoon
features.description: A huge barrier reef ring 60 km across enclosing a lagoon with several high volcanic islands in the middle. Its floor holds over 60 Japanese ships sunk in Operation Hailstone (1944), making it the world's top wreck dive.
features.look_for: Large reef ring with green islands in the middle

features.name: Chesterfield Islands
features.description: A vast reef complex in the Coral Sea 550 km northwest of New Caledonia, its reef rim forming a huge partial ring around a 3,500 km² lagoon with tiny sand cays. It is uninhabited apart from seabirds and turtles.
features.look_for: Huge partial reef ring in open sea

features.name: Hala Lake
features.description: An isolated lake in a high basin of the Qilian Shan at 4,077 m, with glaciers on the ridges around it; in Google imagery it shows as a bright white disk (ice and salt). It is a closed basin lake ringed by old shorelines.
features.look_for: Pale white oval lake in barren high basin

verified.note: lake appears white (frozen/saline) in Google imagery; very distinct

features.name: Gulf Country salt flats (Karumba)
features.description: A broad band of dazzling white salt pans and mudflats along the south-east Gulf of Carpentaria near Karumba, laced by tidal creeks. They flood in the wet season and bake white in the dry.
features.look_for: Bright white saltpan band behind the coast

features.name: Tinian North Field
features.description: The vast WWII airfield on Tinian, with four parallel 2.6 km runways cut into the jungle, from which the Enola Gay and Bockscar flew to Hiroshima and Nagasaki in 1945. It was the busiest airport in the world in 1945.
features.look_for: Parallel runways on island tip

features.name: Ras Nouadhibou
features.description: A slender 50 km finger of desert pointing south into the Atlantic, enclosing the sheltered Bay of Lévrier. The Mauritania–Western Sahara border runs straight down its spine.
features.look_for: Thin desert peninsula pointing south

features.name: Sturt Stony Desert
features.description: A plain of shining gibber stones with patches of dunes and pale clay pans, near the Queensland-SA border. The polished desert pavement made the 1840s expedition of Charles Sturt so difficult that his horses' hooves wore down.
features.look_for: Mottled pale-and-rust plain with dune patches

features.name: Rondônia deforestation fishbone
features.description: Deforestation along the BR-364 highway in Rondônia makes a classic "fishbone": side roads cut perpendicular into the rainforest every few kilometers, each fringed with cleared plots.
features.look_for: Herringbone clearings

features.name: Cape Flattery silica dunes
features.description: Brilliant white parabolic dunes streaking across Cape Flattery on Cape York, made of almost pure silica sand. It is the world's largest silica sand mine, shipping glass-making sand to Asia.
features.look_for: White parallel dune streaks on green cape

features.name: Bering Glacier
features.description: The largest glacier in continental North America, a 190 km river of ice whose terminal lobe slumps into the iceberg-choked Vitus Lake. It surges every few decades, advancing kilometers in a year.
features.look_for: Broad ice lobe ending in a meltwater lake (Vitus Lake) by the sea

features.name: Canterbury Plains
features.description: New Zealand's largest plain, a patchwork of fields and circular centre-pivot irrigation sliced by pale braided rivers running from the Alps. Irrigated dairy farming has spread rapidly here.
features.look_for: Green fields with circles crossed by braided rivers

features.name: Disko Island
features.description: A brooding basalt plateau island capped by its own ice caps, its cliffs layered in horizontal lava flows; Earth's only place with large masses of native terrestrial iron.
features.look_for: Dark plateau island with ice caps and stepped cliffs

features.name: Hardangerjøkulen
features.description: Norway's sixth-largest glacier, an isolated white cap on the bleak Hardangervidda plateau; the ice planet Hoth scenes of The Empire Strikes Back were filmed here.
features.look_for: Isolated ice cap on a lake-dotted plateau

verified.note: isolated ice cap on lake plateau

features.name: Ord River irrigation area
features.description: Rectangular green and brown irrigated fields clustered along the Ord River below Lake Argyle, a sharp patch of geometry in the empty Kimberley. Sugar, melons and sandalwood are grown here.
features.look_for: Green field grid beside a river in brown savanna

features.name: El Pinacate Volcanic Field
features.description: A black lava field with over 400 cinder cones and ten giant maars like El Elegante (1.6 km across), next to a sea of sand. Apollo astronauts trained here.
features.look_for: Dark volcanic shield pitted with cinder cones and huge round maar craters

features.name: Great Sea Reef
features.description: Fiji's Cakaulevu, one of the longest barrier reef systems in the world, tracing a 200 km arc off the north coast of Vanua Levu. From above it is a faint pale line of reef separating a shallow green lagoon from deep blue.
features.look_for: Long faint reef line off a big island

features.name: Lake Gregory (Paraku)
features.description: A cluster of blue and jade lakes in the red sand of the Great Sandy Desert, fed by the Sturt Creek floods. When full it is one of the most important inland waterbird refuges in Australia.
features.look_for: Green-blue lakes on red desert with white fringes

features.name: Bunda Cliffs
features.description: Sheer limestone cliffs up to 120 m high where the treeless Nullarbor Plain drops into the Great Australian Bight, running nearly unbroken for about 100 km. From space they form one of the straightest coastlines on Earth.
features.look_for: Straight cliff coast at the edge of a flat plain

features.name: Scott Reef
features.description: Two large oceanic reefs on the edge of the Timor Sea: South Scott Reef is a near-perfect ring around a deep lagoon, and North Scott Reef a crescent. They rise from deep water on the edge of the continental shelf.
features.look_for: Big circular turquoise atoll ring in deep blue

features.name: Majuro
features.description: The capital atoll of the Marshall Islands, a skinny 50 km-long ring of islets around a deep lagoon, with the town packed along its eastern arm. One road runs almost its whole length, rarely more than a few hundred metres wide.
features.look_for: Long thin atoll ring around a deep lagoon

verified.note: shifted center to feature seen in check image

features.name: Noor Ouarzazate Solar Complex
features.description: One of the world's largest concentrated solar plants: a glinting circle of heliostat mirrors around a central tower beside acres of trough collectors. It covers about 30 km² of desert.
features.look_for: Mirror circle and grid of solar troughs

features.name: Lac Télé
features.description: A near-perfect oval lake about 5 km across, sunk in unbroken swamp forest in northern Congo-Brazzaville. Its odd round shape has prompted theories that it is an impact crater, and cryptozoologists hunted a 'dinosaur' here.
features.look_for: Dark oval in unbroken green forest

features.name: Southwest Kansas Center Pivots
features.description: Tens of thousands of center pivots over the Ogallala Aquifer turn southwest Kansas into a lattice of 800 m circles, some of the most striking crop geometry on Earth.
features.look_for: Dense grid of green and tan circles covering the plains

verified.note: pivot circles, somewhat muted in this imagery

features.name: Lake Paniai
features.description: The largest of the Wissel Lakes, a dark lake in a broad highland basin at 1,750 m in Indonesian Papua, with smaller lakes Tigi and Tage nearby. The lakes were unknown to the outside world until a 1936 flight spotted them.
features.look_for: Dark highland lake with smaller lakes nearby

features.name: Sognefjord
features.description: Norway's longest and deepest fjord, a dark blue crack running 205 km inland with branches like Nærøyfjord; the water is 1,300 m deep beneath cliffs 1,000 m high.
features.look_for: Long branching dark fjord into snowy highlands

verified.note: wiki point at fjord mouth; label moved to mid-fjord

features.name: Salpausselkä ridges
features.description: Two parallel moraine ridges marking where the ice sheet paused ~12,000 years ago; they arc across south Finland, damming the Lakeland behind them.
features.look_for: Long curved ridges with lakes on the north side

verified.note: ridges visible only as arcs bounding lake country

features.name: Bełchatów mine
features.description: One of Europe's largest lignite pits, a vast terraced crater feeding the continent's biggest coal-fired power plant, with the spoil mountain Kamieńsk.
features.look_for: Huge terraced brown pit with a power station

features.name: Mount Veniaminof
features.description: A massive stratovolcano with an 8 km caldera filled by a glacier, with an active cinder cone poking through the ice. It has one of the largest summit ice fields on any Alaskan volcano.
features.look_for: Ice-filled caldera, an oval white bowl on the Alaska Peninsula

features.name: Cape Krusenstern Beach Ridges
features.description: Some 114 successive beach ridges record 5,000 years of shoreline growth on the Chukchi Sea, each with archaeological sites of the people who camped on it.
features.look_for: Fan of more than 100 parallel beach ridges beside a lagoon

features.name: Pompey Reefs
features.description: A maze of reefs on the outer Great Barrier Reef dissected by deep channels that look like ink drawings, among the most intricate reef patterns on the planet. Strong tidal currents scour the channels between the reefs.
features.look_for: Lacy maze of reefs split by deep channels

features.name: Tuktoyaktuk Peninsula Lakes
features.description: A low tundra coast so densely packed with thermokarst lakes that it is more water than land. It hosts the world's densest concentration of pingos, including 49 m Ibyuk.
features.look_for: Coast shredded into thousands of round thaw lakes, some breached by the sea

features.name: Victoria Island Lake Country
features.description: The world's eighth largest island is scoured by ice-age flow into parallel drumlins and elongated lakes. It contains a lake on an island in a lake on an island in a lake on an island.
features.look_for: Streaked terrain of drumlins and aligned lakes on a huge arctic island

features.name: Sheep Mountain Anticline
features.description: A textbook doubly plunging anticline in the Bighorn Basin, its concentric strata like the hull of an overturned boat; geology field courses come here from around the world.
features.look_for: Canoe-shaped striped fold of rock layers cut by a river

features.name: Grasberg mine
features.description: An immense terraced pit high in the Sudirman Range at about 4,000 m, ringed by grey rock and waste piles. It holds one of the world's largest gold and copper reserves; open-pit mining ended in 2019 and moved underground.
features.look_for: Huge grey stepped pit in barren mountains

features.name: Russell Glacier & Sandflugtdalen
features.description: A lobe of the ice sheet edge east of Kangerlussuaq, where a grey glacier wall meets braided meltwater rivers and wind-blown sand flats.
features.look_for: Ice sheet edge with braided grey rivers and sand

features.name: Jökulsárlón & Breiðamerkurjökull
features.description: A glacier lagoon full of floating icebergs where Breiðamerkurjökull calves; the lagoon has grown rapidly as the glacier retreats.
features.look_for: Lagoon with white icebergs at a glacier tongue

features.name: San Francisco Volcanic Field
features.description: Around 600 volcanoes dot this field north of Flagstaff, including the San Francisco Peaks and black Sunset Crater, which erupted around 1085 AD.
features.look_for: Dozens of dark cinder cones and black lava flows around a big snowy peak

verified.note: dark cinder cones and forested peaks

features.name: Hill Inlet & Whitehaven Beach
features.description: A tidal inlet on Whitsunday Island where white silica sand and turquoise water swirl together in shifting patterns; Whitehaven Beach stretches 7 km south of it. The sand is 98% pure silica.
features.look_for: Swirling white sand and turquoise inlet

features.name: Henderson Island
features.description: An uninhabited raised coral island, the largest in the Pitcairn group, with flat-topped cliffs and dense forest. It is a World Heritage site, also notorious for its beaches littered with plastic.
features.look_for: Flat green raised island in deep sea

features.name: Penrhyn (Tongareva)
features.description: The largest and most remote atoll of the Cook Islands, a pale reef necklace around a deep 233 km² lagoon speckled with coral heads. It was once a source of natural pearls and mother-of-pearl shell.
features.look_for: Big reef ring with dotted lagoon

features.name: Prince Christian Sound
features.description: A narrow, winding sound threading Greenland's southern tip past sheer granite walls and hanging glaciers, cutting off Cape Farewell's islands.
features.look_for: Narrow winding channel through steep icy mountains

features.name: Qarhan Salt Lake
features.description: A vast salt playa in the Qaidam Basin, its southern side carved into dazzling turquoise, green and white potash evaporation ponds. The Qarhan salt crust is so thick that a 32 km road and railway run on it.
features.look_for: Turquoise rectangles on white salt crust

features.name: Yellowstone Caldera
features.description: A 45 x 85 km caldera from an eruption 640,000 years ago. Its geyser basins include Grand Prismatic Spring, whose rainbow mats of microbes ring a 110 m pool.
features.look_for: Forested plateau with a large lake and pale thermal basins

verified.note: Yellowstone Lake and forested plateau; caldera itself subtle

features.name: Watkins Range & Gunnbjørn Fjeld
features.description: Dark nunataks poking through the ice near the East Greenland coast, including Gunnbjørn Fjeld (3,694 m), the highest point of the Arctic.
features.look_for: Dark rocky peaks emerging from white ice

features.name: Entrecasteaux Reefs
features.description: A chain of remote atolls north of New Caledonia (Huon, Surprise, Fabre, Le Leizour), crisp reef rings in deep blue water. They are major nesting sites for green turtles and part of a World Heritage site.
features.look_for: Chain of crisp reef rings in deep blue

features.name: Wadden Sea
features.description: The world's largest unbroken system of intertidal sand and mud flats, a 450 km band of channels and shoals behind the Frisian Islands that drains twice a day.
features.look_for: Branching tidal channels in grey-brown mudflats behind barrier islands

features.name: Ball's Pyramid
features.description: An eroded volcanic spike rising 562 m straight out of the sea 20 km from Lord Howe Island, the tallest volcanic stack in the world. A tiny population of the "extinct" Lord Howe stick insect was rediscovered on it in 2001.
features.look_for: Lone dark spire with long shadow

features.name: Longyangxia Reservoir
features.description: A sprawling dendritic reservoir on the upper Yellow River, flanked by the world's largest hydro-solar hybrid park, a dark blanket of panels on the grassland. The solar park covers over 20 km2.
features.look_for: Branchy blue reservoir next to dark solar-panel blocks

features.name: Westland greenhouses
features.description: One of the densest glasshouse areas on Earth: a solid glittering grey-white carpet of greenhouses between The Hague and Rotterdam.
features.look_for: Continuous shiny grey-white glass roofs

features.name: Hubbard Glacier
features.description: A tidewater glacier with a 10 km calving face that has twice dammed Russell Fjord into a lake. Unlike most Alaskan glaciers it has been advancing for over a century.
features.look_for: Wide striped ice front almost sealing off Russell Fjord

verified.note: calving front at fjord, recentered (patchy imagery)

features.name: Klondike Dredge Tailings
features.description: Gold dredges working the Klondike valleys until 1966 left endless curling windrows of washed gravel, a pattern visible from orbit along Bonanza Creek and the Klondike River.
features.look_for: Worm-like grey gravel ridges filling valley floors

verified.note: pale gravel windrows along valley floors

features.name: Great Salt Lake Causeway Color Split
features.description: A 1959 railroad causeway cut the lake in two; the saltier north arm turned red from halophilic algae and archaea while the south stays blue-green.
features.look_for: A straight line splitting the lake into pink-red north and blue-green south

features.name: Fimiston Super Pit
features.description: Australia's most famous gold mine: a stepped grey pit 3.5 km long beside Kalgoorlie, ringed by waste dumps and tailings dams. It has been worked since the 1890s Golden Mile gold rush.
features.look_for: Huge grey terraced pit beside a town grid

features.name: Rowley Shoals
features.description: Three pear-shaped shelf-edge atolls (Mermaid, Clerke and Imperieuse reefs) lined up 300 km off Broome, glowing turquoise in the deep blue. They are among the most pristine coral reefs in Australian waters.
features.look_for: Three small atoll rings in a line in deep ocean

features.name: Cobourg Peninsula
features.description: A ragged peninsula at the top of Arnhem Land, almost cut off from the mainland, with Port Essington's long drowned inlet probing its centre. It is the site of a failed 1838 British settlement.
features.look_for: Ragged peninsula with a deep inlet

features.name: Aitutaki
features.description: An "almost-atoll" in the Cook Islands: a small green volcanic island perched in the corner of a triangular reef whose lagoon glows in every shade of turquoise. It is often ranked among the most beautiful lagoons on Earth.
features.look_for: Triangle reef with brilliant turquoise lagoon

features.name: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta
features.description: The world's highest coastal range: snowy peaks 5,700 m high just 42 km from the Caribbean beaches, isolated from the Andes.
features.look_for: Isolated triangular massif with white summit patch

verified.note: white summit patch above green, sea nearby

features.name: Roebuck Bay
features.description: A broad bay at Broome whose enormous tides expose vast pale mudflats and a fringe of finger-like red pindan channels. It is one of the most important shorebird feeding grounds on the East Asian flyway.
features.look_for: Turquoise bay with wide white tidal flats and red cliffs

features.name: Nuussuaq Peninsula
features.description: A long, mountainous basalt peninsula between Disko Bay and Uummannaq Fjord, partly ice-capped, like a finger pointing west from the ice sheet.
features.look_for: Mountainous finger of land with small ice caps

features.name: Diavik & Ekati Diamond Mines
features.description: Diavik's pits sit inside dikes built into Lac de Gras, so diamonds are mined from what was the lake bed. The region is a maze of glacially scoured lakes on bare Canadian Shield.
features.look_for: Ringed open pits on an island in an arctic lake

features.name: Ridge-and-Valley Appalachians
features.description: Eroded folds of hard sandstone form long sinuous ridges that zigzag across central Pennsylvania, one of the clearest fold belts visible from space.
features.look_for: Zigzagging parallel forested ridges between farmed valleys

features.name: Pool Malebo
features.description: A lake-like widening of the Congo River dotted with islands, with Kinshasa and Brazzaville on opposite banks, the closest pair of capital cities in the world after Rome and the Vatican.
features.look_for: Wide river lake with sandbanks

features.name: Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam Reservoir
features.description: The new reservoir behind Africa's largest hydroelectric dam, the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, branching up the Blue Nile valley near the Sudanese border.
features.look_for: New branching reservoir

features.name: Qaidam Yardang Field
features.description: One of the largest yardang fields on Earth: tens of thousands of parallel wind-sculpted ridges in the north-western Qaidam Basin, studied as an analogue for Mars. The ridges align with the prevailing north-westerly winds.
features.look_for: Dense fingerprint-like parallel ridges

verified.note: streaky yardang terrain visible at z9; center approximate

features.name: St Austell china clay pits
features.description: Brilliant white kaolin pits and spoil heaps (the 'Cornish Alps') with milky turquoise lakes; the Eden Project domes sit in one old pit.
features.look_for: Bright white pits and heaps with turquoise pools

verified.note: brilliant white pits with turquoise pools

features.name: Rainbow Range
features.description: An eroded shield volcano whose rocks are colored by iron and minerals into bands of red, yellow and purple, standing out vividly from the surrounding green Chilcotin Plateau.
features.look_for: Bare red, orange and lavender hills rising out of dark forest

features.name: Channeled Scablands
features.description: Ice-age floods from Glacial Lake Missoula, repeated dozens of times, scoured anastomosing channels, giant ripples and dry falls into this basalt plain.
features.look_for: Braided dark channels of bare basalt cutting through pale wheat fields

verified.note: pale braided channels in wheat land

features.name: Weipa bauxite mines
features.description: Vivid orange strips of mined bauxite plateau around Weipa on western Cape York, one of the world's largest bauxite deposits. The red-orange cutouts stand out sharply from green savanna and blue estuaries.
features.look_for: Bright orange mining strips near an estuary

features.name: Funafuti
features.description: The capital atoll of Tuvalu: a thread-thin ring of islets around an 18 km-wide lagoon, with the airstrip occupying a big share of the dry land. Its highest point is under 5 m above sea level, making it a symbol of sea-level-rise risk.
features.look_for: Wide lagoon ringed by hairline islets

features.name: Kwajalein Atoll
features.description: One of the largest atolls in the world, a 280 km chain of 97 islands around a vast lagoon. It hosts a US missile test range, used as a target for intercontinental ballistic missiles.
features.look_for: Huge chain of islets around a vast lagoon

verified.note: shifted center to feature seen in check image

features.name: Rongelap Atoll
features.description: A large irregular atoll coated by fallout from the 1954 Castle Bravo test, 180 km away; its people were evacuated in 1985 and most have not returned. The reef rim is visible as a pale outline around a vast lagoon.
features.look_for: Big irregular atoll outline

features.name: Tunulliarfik & South Greenland fjords
features.description: The greenest corner of Greenland, where long fjords like Erik the Red's Tunulliarfik reach glaciers calving icebergs into them.
features.look_for: Long fjords with greenish slopes and glacier ends

features.name: Capricorn and Bunker Group
features.description: Clusters of reefs and coral cays at the southern end of the Great Barrier Reef, including Heron Island, set on arm-like submerged platforms. They are a major turtle nesting area.
features.look_for: Finger-like reef arms with cays

features.name: Bathurst Harbour
features.description: A large dark-tannin estuary in Tasmania's remote Southwest wilderness, reachable only by boat, plane or a long walk. Its tannin-stained water creates a deep-sea habitat in shallow depths.
features.look_for: Dark branching harbour in green wilderness

features.name: Kiritimati
features.description: The world's largest coral atoll by land area, its interior a maze of hundreds of shallow, coloured salt lagoons laced with white coral ridges. Britain and the USA tested nuclear weapons here in 1957-62.
features.look_for: Large atoll with a maze of lagoons

features.name: Bogda Shan
features.description: An isolated glacier-capped spur of the Tian Shan rising to 5,445 m right beside Urumqi and the Turpan Depression. One of the greatest elevation contrasts on Earth: from -154 m in the Turpan Depression to 5,445 m within about 160 km.
features.look_for: White snow ridge between desert basins

features.name: Khavda Renewable Energy Park
features.description: Rows of solar panels being laid over the white salt flat of the Rann of Kutch, set to become the world's largest renewable energy park at over 700 km2. It is so big it is visible from space.
features.look_for: Dark rectangular blocks on white salt flat

features.name: Kangerlussuaq Glacier
features.description: East Greenland's largest outlet glacier, ending in a fjord filled with a jumbled ice mélange; its front retreated ~5 km in 2004-05.
features.look_for: Wide glacier ending in an ice-choked fjord

features.name: Red Deer River Badlands
features.description: Eroded badlands along the Red Deer River expose one of the richest dinosaur fossil beds on Earth, a strip of bare grey ravines amid wheat fields.
features.look_for: Pale gullied badlands cut into flat farmland along a winding river

features.name: Mount Isa mine
features.description: A huge mining complex beside the outback town of Mount Isa, with grey tailings, pits and a tall smelter stack. It is one of the world's most productive mines for lead, silver, copper and zinc.
features.look_for: Grey mine and tailings next to a town in red hills

features.name: Shiretoko Peninsula
features.description: A narrow, mountainous, roadless finger of forest and volcanoes poking into the Sea of Okhotsk, where sea ice reaches its southern limit. It is one of the densest brown bear habitats in the world.
features.look_for: Narrow forested peninsula with volcanic spine

features.name: Scoresby Sund
features.description: The world's largest fjord system: a branching labyrinth of iceberg-dotted channels reaching 350 km into East Greenland around the island Milne Land.
features.look_for: Huge branching fjord with ice-dotted dark water

features.name: Copper River Delta
features.description: A vast wetland built from glacier silt, edged by barrier islands and grey sediment plumes. It is the largest contiguous wetland on the Pacific coast of North America.
features.look_for: Grey glacial silt plume and tidal channels fanning into the Gulf of Alaska

features.name: Mount Whaleback mine
features.description: A giant terraced open pit in the Pilbara at Newman, over 5 km long, cut into a red iron-ore ridge. It is the largest single-pit open-cut iron ore mine in the world.
features.look_for: Elongated stepped pit with dark iron-ore benches in red hills

features.name: King Sound
features.description: A 120 km long gulf in the Kimberley that drains the Fitzroy River, its head filled with brown silty mudflats under some of the largest tides in Australia (up to 11 m). The Buccaneer Archipelago guards its mouth.
features.look_for: Long muddy gulf with brown delta at its head

features.name: Three Parallel Rivers
features.description: The Yangtze, Mekong and Salween flow side by side in deep parallel gorges, less than 70 km apart, before diverging to seas thousands of km apart. Snow ridges divide the gorges.
features.look_for: Three deep parallel N-S river gorges

features.name: Samara Bend
features.description: The Volga swings in a dramatic hairpin around the forested Zhiguli Mountains, the river's most famous loop, clearly visible from orbit.
features.look_for: Tight loop of the Volga around dark forested hills

features.name: Kussharo and Mashu Calderas
features.description: Japan's largest caldera lake, Kussharo, lies next to the tiny steep-walled Lake Mashu, one of the clearest lakes in the world. Atosanupuri's sulfurous vents steam between them.
features.look_for: Big lake with island beside a small round crater lake

features.name: Melville Bay
features.description: A broad bay where the ice sheet reaches the sea along hundreds of km in a continuous procession of glacier fronts and nunataks, one of Greenland's emptiest coasts.
features.look_for: Ice sheet meeting the sea in many glacier tongues

features.name: Sørvágsvatn
features.description: The Faroes' largest lake, which seems to hover above the ocean on Vágar island before spilling over the Bøsdalafossur waterfall into the sea.
features.look_for: Long lake ending at a cliff edge above the sea

features.name: Great Sand Dunes
features.description: The tallest dunes in North America (Star Dune, 230 m) are piled by wind against the Sangre de Cristo Mountains at the edge of the flat San Luis Valley.
features.look_for: Tan sand sea piled against the foot of snowy mountains

features.name: Shelburne Bay dunes
features.description: White parabolic sand dunes stretching inland from Shelburne Bay on Cape York, with perched freshwater lakes in between. Their wind-shaped crescents are bright against tropical heath.
features.look_for: White crescent dunes on dark green coast

features.name: Paektu Mountain
features.description: A stratovolcano on the China-North Korea border with Heaven Lake in its summit caldera, formed in one of the largest eruptions of the past 2,000 years (946 AD). Often snow-covered.
features.look_for: Ring-shaped caldera with blue crater lake

features.name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands
features.description: A horseshoe-shaped atoll of 26 coral islands enclosing a vivid turquoise lagoon in the Indian Ocean. Charles Darwin visited in 1836 and developed his theory of atoll formation here.
features.look_for: Horseshoe atoll with brilliant lagoon

features.name: Savo Island
features.description: A round, forested active volcano island off Guadalcanal, with a summit crater and hot springs. The naval Battle of Savo Island (1942) was fought in the strait nearby, now called Iron Bottom Sound for its sunken ships.
features.look_for: Round green island in dark sea

features.name: Bora Bora
features.description: An eroded volcano rising from one of the world's most famous lagoons, encircled by a reef necklace of sandy motu and turquoise shallows. Its overwater bungalows began a tourism template copied worldwide.
features.look_for: Dark green peak in vivid lagoon inside reef ring

features.name: Maug Islands
features.description: Three thin islands forming the broken rim of a drowned volcanic caldera, enclosing a deep circular bay. Shallow volcanic CO2 vents inside are studied as a natural laboratory for ocean acidification.
features.look_for: Ring of three islands around a round bay

features.name: Pearl River Delta Megalopolis
features.description: The world's largest urban area, a near-continuous grey sprawl of Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Dongguan, Foshan and Hong Kong around a funnel-shaped estuary. Home to some 70 million people.
features.look_for: Vast grey sprawl around a muddy estuary

features.name: Zachariae Isstrøm
features.description: A fast ice stream whose floating front collapsed after 2012; its calving front is a broad arc of shattered ice south of the 79N glacier.
features.look_for: Broken ice front among sea ice

features.name: Denali
features.description: North America's highest peak rises 5,500 m above its surrounding lowlands, one of the greatest base-to-summit reliefs of any mountain on land. Long glaciers like the Kahiltna and Ruth radiate from it.
features.look_for: Massive white massif with radiating glaciers above brown tundra

features.name: Mataiva
features.description: A small atoll whose lagoon is divided by a network of coral ridges into around 70 shallow basins, giving it a striking honeycomb or lattice pattern. Its name means "nine eyes", after its nine passes.
features.look_for: Honeycomb-patterned turquoise lagoon

verified.note: shifted center to feature seen in check image

features.name: Gambier Islands (Mangareva)
features.description: A cluster of high volcanic islands inside a huge reef ring and lagoon, the eroded remnant of an ancient volcano. Mangareva has a 19th-century coral-stone cathedral.
features.look_for: High islands inside a big triangular reef

features.name: Bathurst Island Folds
features.description: Bathurst Island's strata are folded into north-south ridges that stand out vividly in the polar desert; the island was once near the north magnetic pole.
features.look_for: Parallel north-south ridges of folded strata on a barren island

features.name: Foxe Basin Islands & Flats
features.description: A shallow arctic sea studded with low islands and tidal flats, often clogged with sediment-stained ice. It has some of the highest walrus concentrations in the Arctic.
features.look_for: Shallow turquoise water swirling around low limestone islands

verified.note: low islands in shallow water, modest

features.name: Hermit Islands
features.description: A small almost-atoll in the Admiralty Islands: a ring of reef with a few high wooded islands rising inside its lagoon. Its people were nearly wiped out by 19th-century epidemics and plantation labour.
features.look_for: Reef ring with green islands inside

features.name: Xingu Indigenous Park
features.description: A dark-green forest island with straight, surveyed edges, surrounded on all sides by cleared soy and cattle land—one of the starkest deforestation boundaries on Earth.
features.look_for: Green forest island in farmland

features.name: Uummannaq Fjord
features.description: A wide fjord system studded with islands and icebergs from big outlet glaciers like Store Glacier; the heart-shaped granite peak of Uummannaq rises at its center.
features.look_for: Island-studded fjord full of icebergs

features.name: Glacier Bay
features.description: In 1794 Glacier Bay was a single wall of ice; it has since retreated more than 100 km, the fastest glacial retreat on record, revealing a branching fjord system.
features.look_for: Branching fjord system with glaciers at the heads of the arms

features.name: Wapusk Beach Ridges
features.description: Successive shorelines stranded by post-glacial rebound form parallel ridges and lake strings in this polar bear denning area, one of the largest on Earth.
features.look_for: Parallel arcs of raised beaches and lakes along the Hudson Bay shore

verified.note: beach ridges and lakes along coast

features.name: Gros Morne Tablelands
features.description: A slab of Earth's mantle (peridotite) pushed to the surface; its toxic chemistry keeps it almost bare, a desert-like tan block amid Newfoundland's forest.
features.look_for: Barren orange-brown plateau standing out from green forest

features.name: Buccaneer Archipelago
features.description: Some 800 rugged islands scattered across the mouth of King Sound, their drowned ridges forming parallel chains in the sea. Tidal currents race between them at up to 30 km/h.
features.look_for: Swarm of rocky islands in parallel lines

features.name: Franz Josef Glacier
features.description: A steep glacier descending to within 20 km of the Tasman Sea, flowing into temperate rainforest. It has been retreating rapidly since 2008.
features.look_for: White glacier valley above green forest

features.name: Castle Bravo crater
features.description: A crater about 2 km across, blasted into the northwest reef of Bikini Atoll by the 1954 Castle Bravo test, the largest US nuclear explosion. It stands out as a deep blue hole in the pale reef.
features.look_for: Deep blue hole cut into a pale reef

features.name: Barren Island
features.description: South Asia's only active volcano, a small island in the Andaman Sea whose cone sits in a breached caldera with a black lava fan to the sea. It has been erupting on and off since 1991.
features.look_for: Small island with central cone and dark lava fan

features.name: Aletsch Glacier
features.description: The largest glacier in the Alps, a 20 km curving river of ice with dark medial moraine stripes, flowing from Konkordiaplatz below the Jungfrau.
features.look_for: Long curving ice river with dark stripes

features.name: Kalahari Linear Dunes
features.description: Long, red, parallel linear dunes, vegetated and fixed, combing across the southern Kalahari for hundreds of kilometres. Their spacing is remarkably regular, like corduroy.
features.look_for: Red parallel dune lines

features.name: Badain Jaran Desert
features.description: Home to the tallest stationary dunes on Earth (up to 500 m), with over 100 small turquoise lakes tucked between the megadunes. Groundwater feeds the lakes despite almost no rainfall.
features.look_for: Giant orange dune ridges with tiny blue-green lakes

features.name: Laki craters
features.description: A 27 km line of 130 craters that in 1783 poured out one of history's largest lava floods, killing a fifth of Iceland's population and cooling the Northern Hemisphere.
features.look_for: Line of small craters running NE-SW, mossy lava fields

features.name: Salar de Uyuni
features.description: The world's largest salt flat: a dazzling 10,000 km² white sheet on the Altiplano at 3,650 m, so flat it is used to calibrate satellite altimeters.
features.look_for: Huge brilliant-white pan with dark island specks

verified.note: salar fills frame left of center; recentered on pan

features.name: Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon
features.description: The Yarlung Tsangpo swings around Namcha Barwa in a dramatic U-turn through the deepest canyon on Earth (up to 6 km deep). Below it, it becomes the Brahmaputra.
features.look_for: River making tight hairpin through forested mountains

features.name: Vermilion Cliffs & Paria Plateau
features.description: Towering red escarpments edge the Paria Plateau, where crossbedded dune sandstone forms the swirled patterns of Coyote Buttes and The Wave.
features.look_for: Red cliff walls fronting a swirled sandstone plateau

features.name: Central Florida Lake District
features.description: Dissolving limestone beneath the Florida peninsula has produced thousands of round sinkhole lakes; the Lake Wales Ridge is an ancient sand-dune island.
features.look_for: Hundreds of round sinkhole lakes scattered across a sandy ridge

features.name: Manasarovar and Rakshastal
features.description: Two blue lakes side by side below Mount Kailash: round, 'holy' Manasarovar and crescent-shaped, saline Rakshastal, the 'demon lake'. They are joined by a short channel.
features.look_for: Pair of blue lakes, round and crescent

features.name: Snæfellsjökull
features.description: A neat glacier-capped stratovolcano at the tip of the Snæfellsnes peninsula, the entrance to Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth.
features.look_for: Small white ice cap at the tip of a peninsula

features.name: Chatham Island & Te Whanga Lagoon
features.description: A large lagoon covering a fifth of Chatham Island, separated from the sea by a narrow sand barrier. The Chathams are the first inhabited land to see the sunrise.
features.look_for: Big lagoon inside a T-shaped island

features.name: Bureya Reservoir
features.description: A narrow, sinuous reservoir winding north through the Bureya mountains of the Far East. In 2018 a giant landslide dammed it, creating a striking scar that had to be blasted through.
features.look_for: Thin winding water through mountains

verified.note: thin winding reservoir, faint at z8

features.name: Dakhla Peninsula
features.description: A 40 km hook of sand curling south-west off the Saharan coast, enclosing a shallow turquoise lagoon (Dakhla Bay). Kite-surfers love the flat lagoon water.
features.look_for: Curving sand spit and lagoon

features.name: Barotse Floodplain
features.description: A 200 km-long pale floodplain along the upper Zambezi laced with oxbows and channels, drowned every wet season. The Lozi king leaves it by royal barge in the annual Kuomboka ceremony.
features.look_for: Pale floodplain with channels

features.name: Mingsha Shan Dunes
features.description: Star dunes up to 250 m tall pile up against the oasis of Dunhuang, with the Crescent Lake hidden among them. The edge between irrigated fields and sand is razor-sharp.
features.look_for: Sharp edge between green oasis and tall dunes

features.name: North Bohemian lignite basin
features.description: Giant pits (ČSA, Bílina, Vršany) below the Ore Mountains have devoured towns including old Most, leaving brown terraces and new lakes.
features.look_for: Large brown terraced pits below a forested scarp

features.name: Devon Ice Cap
features.description: One of the largest ice caps in the Canadian Arctic, about 14,000 km2. The rest of Devon Island is the largest uninhabited island on Earth, a brown polar desert used as a Mars analog.
features.look_for: Large white dome covering eastern Devon Island

verified.note: ice cap on east Devon Island; recentered

features.name: Bonneville Salt Flats
features.description: A 120 km2 salt pan left by ice-age Lake Bonneville, so flat that land speed records are set on it; a racetrack is graded on the crust each summer.
features.look_for: Blinding white salt crust beside dark desert mountains

verified.note: white crust NE of frame center; recentered

features.name: Powder River Basin Coal Mines
features.description: The world's largest coal mines, North Antelope Rochelle and Black Thunder, peel back the prairie to expose seams 20 m thick.
features.look_for: Long black open-cut strips and grey spoil piles in the prairie

features.name: Gove bauxite mine
features.description: Patches of brick-red bare earth on the Gove Peninsula where bauxite is strip-mined, striking against green woodland. The mine and former alumina refinery support the town of Nhulunbuy.
features.look_for: Orange-red mining patches in green bush

features.name: Juyan Lake Basin
features.description: The terminal lakes of the Ruo Shui (Black River) in the Alxa desert, partly revived after decades of being dry. Ruins of the Tangut city of Khara-Khoto lie nearby.
features.look_for: Shallow lakes at the end of a river fan in desert

verified.note: recentered north onto the white flats/lakes

features.name: Mýrdalsjökull
features.description: An ice cap on Iceland's south coast hiding Katla, one of Iceland's most dangerous volcanoes; its eruptions send floods across the black sands below.
features.look_for: White ice cap above black sand plains

features.name: Curonian Spit
features.description: A 98 km sand spit only a few hundred metres wide, crested with Europe's highest drifting dunes, separating the Curonian Lagoon from the Baltic.
features.look_for: Hair-thin curved sand strip enclosing a lagoon

features.name: Łeba moving dunes
features.description: Bare white dunes up to 40 m high marching inland at 10 m a year in Słowiński National Park, between the Baltic and Lake Łebsko.
features.look_for: White dune patch between sea and lake

features.name: Guadalupe Mountains & Salt Basin
features.description: The Guadalupe Mountains are an exhumed Permian reef; at their base lie white salt flats and gypsum dunes.
features.look_for: Limestone escarpment with white salt flats and gypsum dunes at its western foot

features.name: Mississippi Meanders & Oxbows
features.description: Between Memphis and Vicksburg the river meanders so actively that abandoned loops form dozens of oxbow lakes, like Lake Chicot and Lake Washington.
features.look_for: Tight river loops and crescent oxbow lakes in a flat green plain

features.name: Guerrero Negro Salt Works
features.description: The largest salt works in the world, around 300 km2 of solar evaporation ponds beside Ojo de Liebre lagoon, where grey whales calve each winter.
features.look_for: Enormous grid of pink, turquoise and white evaporation ponds by a lagoon

features.name: Ninety Mile Beach & Te Paki dunes
features.description: A straight 88 km beach along the west coast of the North Island's tip, with giant pale sand dunes at Te Paki. The beach is an official highway.
features.look_for: Long straight beach and pale dunes

features.name: Lake Grassmere salt works
features.description: A shallow coastal lake in Marlborough turned into pink and green evaporation ponds, New Zealand's only solar salt works. The pinks come from algae and brine shrimp.
features.look_for: Pink and green ponds by the coast

features.name: Öræfajökull
features.description: Iceland's highest volcano (Hvannadalshnúkur 2,110 m), a southern dome of Vatnajökull whose glacier tongues spill toward the coast.
features.look_for: Ice-covered volcano with tongues spilling to lowland

features.name: Saimaa lake maze
features.description: Finland's largest lake is a fractal labyrinth of 14,000 islands and narrow sounds with 15,000 km of shoreline, home to the rare Saimaa ringed seal.
features.look_for: Fractal tangle of water and forested islands

verified.note: label moved from wiki point into the main lake maze

features.name: Teide & Las Cañadas
features.description: Spain's highest peak (3,718 m) rises from a 16 km caldera floored with multicoloured lava flows; Earth's third-tallest volcanic structure from the ocean floor.
features.look_for: Large caldera with a central cone and dark lava fans

features.name: K'gari (Fraser Island)
features.description: The world's largest sand island, 120 km long, with forests growing on sand and over 100 freshwater lakes perched in the dunes. Its long eastern surf beach is used as a highway.
features.look_for: Long sand island with pale dune blowouts

features.name: Wilpena Pound
features.description: A natural oval amphitheatre 17 km long in the Flinders Ranges, enclosed by a rim of tilted quartzite ridges. It is a synclinal basin, not a crater, and is sacred to the Adnyamathanha people.
features.look_for: Oval ring of ridges enclosing a basin

features.name: Lac de Yaté
features.description: New Caledonia's largest reservoir, a dark branching lake flooded into red lateritic hills of the Grand Sud, created by the Yaté dam in 1959. Drowned forest still stands in parts of it.
features.look_for: Dark branching lake in red-brown hills

features.name: Lop Nur Potash Evaporation Ponds
features.description: A huge grid of brine evaporation ponds in turquoise, white and green, laid out on the salt crust of the former Lop Nur lakebed. It is one of the world's largest potash sulfate operations.
features.look_for: Rectilinear turquoise pond grid on white salt

verified.note: recentered on pond grid (seen NW of first shot center)

features.name: Yellow River Delta
features.description: A young, fast-growing delta pushing into the Bohai Sea, with a single muddy channel, fresh mudflats and grids of salt pans and fish ponds. Much of it formed after the river shifted here in 1855.
features.look_for: Muddy lobe into the sea with geometric ponds

features.name: Hallasan
features.description: A broad shield volcano forming nearly all of Jeju Island, its summit crater lake Baengnokdam ringed by forest and hundreds of small parasitic cones (oreum). South Korea's highest peak at 1,950 m.
features.look_for: Dark forested dome centered on an oval island

features.name: Mount Conner
features.description: A flat-topped horseshoe-shaped mesa rising 300 m from the plain east of Uluru, ringed by an apron of scree and a faint halo of outwash. Travellers often mistake it for Uluru.
features.look_for: Flat-topped mesa with a broad pale apron

features.name: Mount Tongariro & Ngauruhoe
features.description: A complex of volcanic cones and craters including the symmetrical cone of Ngauruhoe and the colourful Emerald Lakes. It became New Zealand's first national park in 1887.
features.look_for: Brown volcanic massif with craters

features.name: Whakaari / White Island
features.description: An active andesite volcano island in the Bay of Plenty with a pale steaming crater and acidic crater lake open to the sea. A 2019 eruption killed 22 tourists.
features.look_for: Small grey island with a pale crater

features.name: Mount Everest
features.description: Earth's highest summit (8,849 m), a pyramid of rock and ice feeding the Khumbu and Rongbuk glaciers. Its north face drops into Tibet, its south side into Nepal.
features.look_for: Star-shaped ice massif with long debris-covered glaciers

features.name: Zanda Earth Forest
features.description: A vast labyrinth of eroded lakebed sediments along the Sutlej valley, carved into towering earth pillars and fins. Ruins of the Guge kingdom are cut into its cliffs.
features.look_for: Intricately dissected tan badlands along a river

features.name: Kvitøya
features.description: 'White Island': almost entirely covered by a single smooth ice cap, a white oval in the Arctic Ocean where Andrée's 1897 balloon expedition met its end.
features.look_for: Isolated white ice-covered island

features.name: Żelazny Most tailings pond
features.description: Europe's largest tailings reservoir, a 14 km² dammed lake of copper-mine waste, light grey with a bright pool.
features.look_for: Large rectangular-ish grey pond with dam walls

verified.note: round turquoise tailings pond, very high contrast

features.name: Great Salt Lake Mineral Ponds
features.description: Industrial evaporation ponds on the Great Salt Lake's shore concentrate brine for potash, magnesium and salt, forming bright geometric patches of color.
features.look_for: Geometric ponds in vivid turquoise, red and cream

features.name: Ashmore Reef
features.description: A wide oval shelf-edge reef with turquoise sand flats and three tiny islets, halfway between Australia and Timor. It is a nature reserve important for seabirds and sea snakes.
features.look_for: Turquoise oval reef platform in deep ocean

features.name: Macquarie Harbour
features.description: A long dark harbour in western Tasmania, six times larger than Sydney Harbour, entered only through the narrow Hells Gates. It hosted one of Australia's harshest convict prisons.
features.look_for: Long dark inlet behind a narrow entrance

features.name: New Caledonia Barrier Reef
features.description: The world's second-longest double barrier reef, enclosing a vast turquoise lagoon around Grande Terre. It is a World Heritage site.
features.look_for: Turquoise lagoon outlined by reef around a long island

features.name: Tengger Caldera
features.description: A 16 km caldera with a flat 'sea of sand' floor out of which rise the smoking Bromo crater and the ribbed cone of Batok. Semeru, Java's highest peak, smokes just to the south.
features.look_for: Round caldera with grey sand floor and inner cones

features.name: Independence Fjord
features.description: A 200 km straight fjord cutting into far-north Greenland, often frozen white between bare red-brown cliffs.
features.look_for: Long straight fjord, frozen white, in brown desert

features.name: Wolstenholme Fjord
features.description: A fjord near Pituffik where several glaciers spill from the ice sheet side by side, with flat-topped Mount Dundas at its mouth.
features.look_for: Fjord fed by several parallel glacier tongues

features.name: Great Glen
features.description: A dead-straight fault valley slicing Scotland in two from Inverness to Fort William, strung with Loch Ness, Loch Oich and Loch Lochy.
features.look_for: Ruler-straight valley of thin lochs across the Highlands

features.name: Mackenzie River Delta
features.description: Canada's largest delta, a 13,000 km2 maze of channels and some 49,000 lakes on permafrost. Pingos, ice-cored hills up to 50 m high, dot the nearby Tuktoyaktuk Peninsula.
features.look_for: Huge fan of channels and countless lakes entering the Beaufort Sea

features.name: Axel Heiberg Ice Caps
features.description: The Müller and Steacie ice caps cover the mountainous core of Axel Heiberg; the island also hosts a fossil forest of 45-million-year-old mummified trees.
features.look_for: Mountainous island with ice caps spilling long valley glaciers

features.name: Snake River Plain Pivots
features.description: Center-pivot potato and grain fields irrigated from the Snake River and the Snake River Aquifer polka-dot this lava plain.
features.look_for: Hundreds of green circles on a brown volcanic plain

verified.note: pivot circles along the Snake near Burley/Rupert, recentered

features.name: Nebraska Sand Hills
features.description: The largest dune field in the Western Hemisphere, 50,000 km2 of grass-stabilized sand dunes with thousands of small lakes fed by the Ogallala Aquifer.
features.look_for: Rolling grassy dunes with scattered lakes and pivots

verified.note: dune ridges with small lakes clear at z10

features.name: Coongie Lakes
features.description: Green freshwater lakes fed by the Cooper Creek's north-west branch, a striking oasis set between parallel red dunes in the Strzelecki Desert. They are a Ramsar wetland of international importance.
features.look_for: Green lakes amid parallel red dunes

features.name: Pukapuka
features.description: A distinctive Y- or boomerang-shaped atoll in the northern Cook Islands, with three islets at its corners and a lagoon full of coral heads. Its isolation produced a unique language and culture.
features.look_for: Y-shaped atoll with mottled lagoon

features.name: Iguaçu & Iguazú National Parks
features.description: A dark-green block of Atlantic forest with knife-edge borders, surrounded on the Brazilian side by bare farmland.
features.look_for: Forest block with sharp straight edges

features.name: Nares Strait
features.description: A narrow channel, at places just 35 km wide, separating Greenland from Ellesmere Island; sea-ice arches and floes jam it most of the year.
features.look_for: Narrow strait between two Arctic landmasses, often ice-filled

features.name: Beerenberg
features.description: The world's northernmost active subaerial volcano, a glacier-draped cone forming the end of remote Jan Mayen island with ice tongues radiating to the sea.
features.look_for: Ice-capped cone at the end of a lonely island

features.name: Santorini caldera
features.description: A drowned caldera ringed by cliff-edged island fragments, with dark lava islets of Nea Kameni at its center - remnant of the Bronze Age Minoan eruption.
features.look_for: Ring of island fragments with dark central islet

features.name: Nauru
features.description: A small raised coral island whose interior plateau has been strip-mined for phosphate, leaving a grey-white field of jagged coral pinnacles inside a green coastal ring. It is the world's smallest island republic.
features.look_for: Small round island with a pale ravaged interior

features.name: Batagaika Crater
features.description: A rapidly expanding thermokarst slump, the 'gateway to the underworld': a 1 km tadpole-shaped scar where the permafrost is thawing and collapsing.
features.look_for: Pale tadpole-shaped scar in dark forest

features.name: Ogasawara Islands
features.description: Remote subtropical islands 1,000 km south of Tokyo that have never been connected to a continent, called the 'Galapagos of the Orient'. Turquoise reefs ring the green islands.
features.look_for: Small green islands in deep blue ocean

features.name: Biafo-Hispar Glaciers
features.description: Two great glaciers meeting at the Hispar La form a 100 km ice highway, the longest outside the polar regions. Snow Lake at their junction is a vast basin of ice.
features.look_for: Very long glaciers meeting at a high ice basin

features.name: Reykjanes lava fields
features.description: Repeated fissure eruptions since 2021 (Fagradalsfjall, Sundhnúkur) have covered the peninsula near Grindavík with fresh black lava.
features.look_for: Fresh black lava flows over moss-green older lava

features.name: Minas de Riotinto
features.description: 5,000 years of mining have left multicoloured open pits (Corta Atalaya) and a blood-red, acidic river, the Río Tinto, used by NASA as a Mars analogue.
features.look_for: Red, ochre and green pits and spoil heaps

features.name: Waterpocket Fold
features.description: A 160 km wrinkle in the Earth's crust (monocline) where rock layers bend sharply, eroded into a stripe of white, red and grey bands in Capitol Reef.
features.look_for: Long tilted stripe of colored rock layers running north-south

verified.note: colorful N-S stripe clear at z10

features.name: Lake Dundas
features.description: A cluster of pale salt pans among the dark eucalypt woodlands south of Norseman, forming a long white chain. The surrounding Great Western Woodlands are the largest intact temperate woodland on Earth.
features.look_for: White salt patches in dark green woodland

features.name: Mount Tarawera & Lake Rotomahana
features.description: A volcanic massif split by a 17 km rift from its 1886 eruption, which destroyed the famous Pink and White Terraces. The rift forms a line of craters and the lake.
features.look_for: Pale rift scar across a massif

features.name: Ross Ice Shelf
features.description: The largest ice shelf on Earth, a floating plate the size of France; its seaward edge is a 600 km ice cliff up to 50 m high.
features.look_for: Flat white sheet ending at a cliff line

verified.note: not image-checked: Natural Earth geometry / continental-scale feature

features.name: Erg Chebbi
features.description: A compact sea of tall orange dunes, up to 150 m high, sitting like a spilled heap of paprika on dark stony hamada at Morocco's edge. Its sharp boundary against the black plain makes it pop.
features.look_for: Small orange dune patch on dark plain

features.name: Hálslón
features.description: A long glacial-silt reservoir behind Kárahnjúkar Dam, Europe's tallest concrete-face dam, feeding Iceland's biggest hydro plant.
features.look_for: Long milky turquoise reservoir in barren highland

features.name: Van Mijenfjorden
features.description: A long fjord almost sealed off by the island Akseløya at its mouth, so it freezes earlier and stays ice-covered longer than its neighbours.
features.look_for: Long fjord with an island plugging its mouth

features.name: Mont Blanc massif
features.description: Western Europe's highest mountains, a white wall of ice with long glaciers like the Mer de Glace pouring into Chamonix's valley.
features.look_for: Big white ice massif with long glaciers

features.name: Tajogaite lava field
features.description: La Palma's 2021 eruption, Spain's most destructive in history, sent a black lava apron to the sea, burying 3,000 buildings.
features.look_for: Fresh black lava tongue to the sea

verified.note: dark fresh lava on west flank

features.name: Moorea
features.description: A heart-shaped volcanic island with two deep fjord-like bays, Cook's Bay and Opunohu Bay, cutting into its north shore. It is the remnant of a volcano that collapsed about 1.5 million years ago.
features.look_for: Heart-shaped island with two northern bays

features.name: Banc d'Arguin
features.description: A vast zone of turquoise shallows, sandbanks and low islands where the Sahara meets the Atlantic. It is one of the world's great wintering grounds for shorebirds.
features.look_for: Pale turquoise shoals off a desert coast

features.name: Bazaruto Archipelago
features.description: Islands made of high sand dunes off Mozambique, surrounded by swirling turquoise shallows, sandbars and seagrass. Home to the last viable dugong population in East Africa.
features.look_for: Dune islands and shallows

features.name: Annapurna Massif
features.description: A 55 km wall of snowy peaks including Annapurna I (8,091 m), cut off by the deep Kali Gandaki gorge from Dhaulagiri. The Annapurna Sanctuary is a glacial amphitheatre within it.
features.look_for: Long snowy massif with a ring-shaped sanctuary

features.name: North Malé Atoll
features.description: The atoll of the capital, Malé, one of the most densely built islands on Earth, with the reclaimed island of Hulhumalé next to it. Its rim of reef faros is distinctive.
features.look_for: Ring of reef patches with a dense city island

features.name: Weda Bay Nickel Industrial Park
features.description: Red-brown nickel laterite mines rapidly stripping Halmahera's forest, with a vast smelter complex on the coast, part of the electric-vehicle battery boom.
features.look_for: Red-brown bare hills and industrial blocks

features.name: Lac de Sainte-Croix & Gorges du Verdon
features.description: A turquoise reservoir at the mouth of the Verdon Gorge, Europe's grandest canyon, whose milky-green river winds between 700 m walls.
features.look_for: Bright turquoise lake and gorge

features.name: Nuup Kangerlua
features.description: Greenland's longest fjord system behind the capital Nuuk, a branching network of dark channels reaching the ice sheet.
features.look_for: Branching fjord system to the ice sheet edge

features.name: Macquarie Island
features.description: A long, narrow sub-Antarctic island made of oceanic crust and mantle rock pushed up above sea level, the only place on Earth where this happens. It is home to millions of penguins.
features.look_for: Thin green-brown island in the Southern Ocean

features.name: Laguna Colorada
features.description: A shallow Altiplano lake stained red-orange by algae and fringed by white borax islands; thousands of James's flamingos feed in its waters.
features.look_for: Rusty red-pink lake with white rims

verified.note: vivid golden-orange lake (Google imagery shows it ochre/red)

features.name: Antofagasta de la Sierra volcanic field
features.description: Black scoria cones and lava flows spill across the pale Puna floor around the oasis village of Antofagasta de la Sierra.
features.look_for: Black cones and flows on pale plain

features.name: Adam's Bridge
features.description: A chain of limestone shoals and sandbanks linking India's Pamban Island to Sri Lanka's Mannar Island across the Palk Strait. Hindu tradition says it was built by Rama's monkey army.
features.look_for: Dotted line of pale shoals across turquoise sea

features.name: Þingvallavatn
features.description: Iceland's largest natural lake, sitting in the rift valley where the North American and Eurasian plates pull apart; fissures run along its northern shore.
features.look_for: Deep blue lake with parallel rift fissures

features.name: Okmok Caldera
features.description: A 10 km circular caldera whose eruption in 43 BC may have chilled the Mediterranean climate at the time of the fall of the Roman Republic. Young cinder cones and lava flows dot its floor.
features.look_for: Huge round caldera filling the end of Umnak Island

features.name: Lake Yamma Yamma
features.description: An ephemeral lake in Queensland's Channel Country with a strongly patterned, swirling clay bed and dark vegetated fringes. It fills only when monsoon floods reach the far south-west.
features.look_for: Pale oval lake bed with swirl patterns

features.name: Lake MacDonnell
features.description: A coastal salt lake on the Eyre Peninsula famous for being split by a causeway into a bubblegum-pink side and an emerald-green side. It is used for gypsum and salt production.
features.look_for: White and pink lake by the coast with green pond

features.name: Pingelap
features.description: A small atoll with three islets where around 10% of people have total colour blindness (achromatopsia), a genetic legacy of a 1775 typhoon bottleneck. Oliver Sacks wrote about it in The Island of the Colorblind.
features.look_for: Small atoll with three islets

features.name: Lop Nur
features.description: The dried terminal lake of the Tarim River left concentric shoreline bands that look like a giant human ear in the desert. China tested its first nuclear bomb nearby in 1964.
features.look_for: Ear-shaped concentric pale rings

verified.note: recentered on the ear rings; unmistakable at z10

features.name: Estonian oil shale mines
features.description: Huge strip mines and grey ash hills of Ida-Viru county, where Estonia burns oil shale for most of its power.
features.look_for: Grey strip-mined land and ash plateaus

verified.note: pits and ash hills east of check centre

features.name: Kaskawulsh Glacier
features.description: Its retreat in 2016 rerouted meltwater from the Slims River to the Kaskawulsh, the first documented case of modern "river piracy" caused by climate change.
features.look_for: Broad glacier with parallel dark moraine stripes

features.name: Lac Guillaume-Delisle
features.description: Also called Richmond Gulf, a 700 km2 tidal lake enclosed by the cuesta cliffs of the Nastapoka arc, with a single narrow outlet where tides race in.
features.look_for: Tidal lake behind a cliff wall connected to Hudson Bay by a narrow gap

features.name: Ungava Lake Plateau
features.description: The treeless Ungava Peninsula is classic Canadian Shield: bedrock scraped clean by ice sheets and dotted with countless lakes aligned with ice flow.
features.look_for: Bare grey rock speckled with thousands of glacially scoured lakes

features.name: Rogers Dry Lake
features.description: This hard-packed lakebed at Edwards Air Force Base serves as a natural runway; the Space Shuttle landed here, and a 1.2 km compass rose is painted on it.
features.look_for: Pale playa marked with giant painted runways and a compass rose

features.name: Lihir (Ladolam) mine
features.description: A gold mine inside a volcanic crater on Lihir Island, open to the sea, where geothermal heat makes the pit dangerously hot. It holds one of the world's largest gold deposits.
features.look_for: Bare brown crater mine by the sea

features.name: Aru Islands
features.description: A group of low islands split by long, narrow river-like channels (sungai) that are actually old river valleys drowned by the sea. They lie on the Sahul shelf between New Guinea and Australia.
features.look_for: Low island crossed by narrow channels

features.name: Caroline Atoll
features.description: A slender, uninhabited atoll of 39 islets in the Line Islands, one of the most pristine in the Pacific. It was renamed Millennium Island as the first land to see the 2000 sunrise.
features.look_for: Thin crescent atoll ring

features.name: Lençóis Maranhenses
features.description: White crescent dunes with thousands of blue and green rainwater lagoons trapped between them every wet season.
features.look_for: White dunes dotted with blue pools

verified.note: white dune field visible even at 195 km

features.name: Mega Rice Project Canals
features.description: A failed 1990s scheme to convert a million hectares of Kalimantan peat swamp into rice fields, leaving a grid of drainage canals that dried the peat and fuelled huge fires.
features.look_for: Long straight canals cutting through peatland

features.name: Upernavik Isstrøm
features.description: A set of four parallel glacier tongues ending side by side in an iceberg-choked fjord north of Upernavik.
features.look_for: Several adjacent glacier fronts with floating ice

features.name: Prins Karls Forland
features.description: A remarkably long, narrow island (86 km by ~10 km) paralleling Spitsbergen's west coast, with a spine of glaciated peaks.
features.look_for: Long thin island parallel to the coast

features.name: Morecambe Bay
features.description: Britain's largest expanse of intertidal flats, 310 km² of sand and channels where the tide comes in 'faster than a galloping horse'.
features.look_for: Huge sandy bay with meandering channels

features.name: Raplee Anticline
features.description: A textbook upfold in which banded limestone layers are curved like a rainbow, cut by the San Juan River near its famous Goosenecks.
features.look_for: Striped arch of grey and red rock bands beside the San Juan River

verified.note: striped arch right of center; recentered

features.name: Carolina Bays
features.description: Half a million oval depressions dot the Atlantic coastal plain; their origin, from wind and water shaping of thaw lakes, was once argued to be a comet swarm.
features.look_for: Hundreds of overlapping elliptical basins all aligned NW-SE

features.name: Lighthouse Reef & Great Blue Hole
features.description: The Great Blue Hole is a 318 m wide, 124 m deep sinkhole formed when sea level was lower; it sits in the lagoon of Lighthouse Reef atoll.
features.look_for: Long turquoise atoll with a perfect dark-blue circle in its lagoon

features.name: Islands of Four Mountains
features.description: A cluster of volcanic islands each made of a near-perfect snowy cone, including frequently erupting Mount Cleveland on the dumbbell-shaped Chuginadak Island.
features.look_for: Row of perfect snowy volcanic cone islands

features.name: Cooper Creek
features.description: A desert river that braids into a broad network of channels and floodplains on its way to Lake Eyre, crossing the red Strzelecki dunes. Burke and Wills died along its banks in 1861.
features.look_for: Pale braided floodplain cutting across red dunes

features.name: Palau Rock Islands
features.description: Hundreds of mushroom-shaped limestone islets inside Palau's great barrier lagoon, with marine lakes such as Jellyfish Lake. They are a World Heritage site.
features.look_for: Swarm of jungle-covered limestone islets inside a big lagoon

features.name: Piton des Neiges and the Cirques
features.description: Piton des Neiges, the highest point in the Indian Ocean (3,070 m), surrounded by three massive eroded cirques: Cilaos, Mafate and Salazie.
features.look_for: Three deep basins in a volcanic island

features.name: Kumtag Desert
features.description: Feathery, pinnate dune patterns sweep across this desert between Lop Nur and Dunhuang, shaped by competing wind directions. Its dark gravel interdunes give it a striking feather-like texture.
features.look_for: Feather-shaped dune ridges, orange on dark gravel

features.name: Salihorsk potash tailings
features.description: Enormous reddish-white salt waste heaps up to 100 m tall around Salihorsk, Belarus's 'Salt Mountains', with brine ponds.
features.look_for: Bright pale-pink heaps and ponds in fields

verified.note: pale salt heaps and brine ponds

features.name: Great Sand Hills
features.description: A 1,900 km2 area of rolling sand hills in Saskatchewan, mostly stabilized by grass but with active dunes, standing out as unplowed land amid grain fields.
features.look_for: Grassy dune field with a few bare blowouts in prairie farmland

features.name: San Francisco Bay Salt Ponds
features.description: Salt ponds tinted by halophilic microbes paint the south bay in rust, pink and chartreuse; many are being restored to tidal marsh.
features.look_for: Patchwork of red, orange and green evaporation ponds at the bay's south end

features.name: Boddington gold mine
features.description: A sprawling grey open pit carved into the forested Darling Range, Australia's largest gold producer. The pit and tailings dams form a stark scar in dark jarrah forest.
features.look_for: Grey multi-lobed pit in dark forest

features.name: Kanton Island
features.description: The largest and only inhabited atoll of the Phoenix Islands, a broad reef ring enclosing a shallow lagoon. It was a Pan Am flying-boat stop on the trans-Pacific route in the 1930s.
features.look_for: Broad lozenge-shaped atoll

features.name: Arno Atoll
features.description: A big Marshallese atoll next to Majuro with an odd outline: a main lagoon plus two long lobes reaching north and east, all edged by a pale reef. Its lagoon arms make it look like a three-armed starfish.
features.look_for: Atoll with long lobed arms

features.name: Mount Ararat
features.description: A huge snow-capped volcanic dome (5,137 m) standing alone above the plains of eastern Turkey, with its smaller twin Little Ararat beside it. Tradition places Noah's Ark on its slopes.
features.look_for: Isolated snowy cone with a smaller twin

features.name: Ordos Loop
features.description: The Yellow River's huge rectangular detour north around the Ordos Plateau, lined with a bright green ribbon of irrigation (the Hetao) against desert. Easy to recognise from orbit as a giant inverted U.
features.look_for: Giant inverted-U river with green irrigated margins

features.name: Bayan Obo Mine
features.description: Two giant open pits with tailings in the Inner Mongolian steppe: the source of nearly half the world's rare-earth elements. Its ore-processing tailings fill a toxic lake near Baotou.
features.look_for: Terraced grey pits in green steppe

features.name: Hpakant Jade Mines
features.description: A vast moonscape of jade mining pits and spoil heaps carved out of the Kachin jungle, the source of most of the world's highest-quality jadeite. Landslides of waste have killed hundreds.
features.look_for: Huge grey-brown scarred area in green jungle

features.name: Colville River Delta
features.description: The largest delta on Alaska's Arctic coast, a fan of braided channels, ice-wedge polygons and lakes. Ice from the river breakup floods its sea ice every spring.
features.look_for: Braided fan of channels and lakes entering the Beaufort Sea

features.name: Thousand Islands
features.description: An archipelago of 1,864 islands of Precambrian granite, the exposed tops of the Frontenac Axis linking the Canadian Shield to the Adirondacks.
features.look_for: Hundreds of tiny islands clustered where Lake Ontario becomes the St. Lawrence

features.name: Bone Valley Phosphate Mines
features.description: Central Florida's phosphate strip mines have dug up hundreds of square kilometres, leaving rectangular lakes and tall white phosphogypsum stacks.
features.look_for: Huge region of square pits, gypsum stacks and settling ponds

features.name: Cerro Prieto Geothermal Ponds
features.description: Brine ponds of one of the largest geothermal fields in the world, sitting on the boundary between the Pacific and North American plates.
features.look_for: Bright evaporation ponds in desert south of Mexicali

features.name: Telfer mine
features.description: A big pale gold-copper mining complex in the empty Great Sandy Desert, its pits and heaps standing out against parallel red dunes. It is one of Australia's most remote major mines.
features.look_for: White-grey mine complex amid red linear dunes

features.name: Wotje Atoll
features.description: A large Ratak-chain atoll with a lumpy reef rim and broad lagoon, used as a fortified Japanese seaplane and air base in WWII. Its smaller neighbour Erikub lies just to the south.
features.look_for: Broad atoll with a smaller atoll beside it

features.name: Godavari Delta
features.description: A lobate delta pushing into the Bay of Bengal, its green paddy fields and mangroves crossed by distributaries, fringed by aquaculture ponds. The river is called the 'Dakshina Ganga' (southern Ganges).
features.look_for: Green delta lobe with branching channels

features.name: Lakes Matano and Towuti
features.description: Ancient tectonic lakes in central Sulawesi, Matano being the deepest in Southeast Asia (590 m). The red laterite scars of the Sorowako nickel mine lie between them.
features.look_for: Two dark lakes with red mine scars nearby

features.name: Hekla
features.description: Iceland's most notorious volcano, an elongated ridge surrounded by fans of dark lava flows; medieval Europeans called it the Gateway to Hell.
features.look_for: Elongated snowy ridge with radiating dark lava flows

verified.note: ridge visible, little snow in summer imagery

features.name: Kerlingarfjöll
features.description: Rhyolite mountains in the highlands streaked orange, yellow and red by geothermal alteration, with steaming vents and snow patches.
features.look_for: Colourful orange-pale mountains with snow streaks

features.name: Bollenstreek tulip fields
features.description: The Dutch flower-bulb district behind the dunes, where in April narrow fields become stripes of red, yellow and purple.
features.look_for: Thin parallel coloured field strips

features.name: Minas Basin Tidal Flats
features.description: The highest tides in the world, up to 16 m, empty and refill this basin twice a day, exposing kilometres of red mud and stirring the water rusty brown.
features.look_for: Brown silt-laden water and red mud flats at the head of the Bay of Fundy

features.name: Mountaintop Removal Mines
features.description: In southern West Virginia whole ridgetops have been blasted away for coal, leaving bare terraced plateaus and filled valleys amid unbroken forest.
features.look_for: Pale flat-topped scars cut into a dark forested plateau

features.name: Mangaia
features.description: A volcanic island ringed by a 1-2 km wide belt of raised fossil reef (makatea), creating a pale rim around darker central hills. It is the oldest island in the Pacific at around 18 million years.
features.look_for: Round island with a pale raised-coral rim

features.name: Kuray Steppe
features.description: Giant current ripples up to 15 m high left by catastrophic Ice-Age floods from a burst glacial lake, still visible across the Kuray basin floor.
features.look_for: Parallel ridges on a basin floor

verified.note: basin visible; ripples not resolvable at this zoom

features.name: San Rafael Glacier & Laguna San Rafael
features.description: A glacier calving into a round tidal lagoon opening to the Pacific, the lowest-latitude tidewater glacier in the world.
features.look_for: Ice tongue into a round lagoon

features.name: Quirimbas Islands
features.description: A string of low coral islands strung along Mozambique's northern coast, edged by turquoise reef flats and mangroves. The old trading town on Ibo island dates to the 16th century.
features.look_for: Chain of coral islands

features.name: Mount Mulanje
