features.description: A massive granite inselberg rising abruptly 2,000 m above the tea estates of southern Malawi, its dark gullied flanks surrounding a high plateau. Its peak, Sapitwa, means 'don't go there'.
features.look_for: Massive dark inselberg

features.name: Danjiangkou Reservoir
features.description: A large two-armed reservoir on the Han River, the starting point of the South-North Water Transfer Project's middle route canal to Beijing. Its jagged shoreline traces drowned valleys.
features.look_for: Branching blue reservoir

features.name: Storstrømmen
features.description: A large surge-type outlet glacier in Northeast Greenland, its smooth lobe spreading into Dove Bugt with flow stripes visible from orbit.
features.look_for: Wide glacier lobe with flow lines

features.name: Isfjorden
features.description: Spitsbergen's largest fjord, branching into arms ringed by bare, layered mountains and glaciers; Longyearbyen lies on its south shore.
features.look_for: Broad branching fjord between brown layered mountains

features.name: Bjørnøya
features.description: Bear Island, a lonely triangular island between Norway and Svalbard, its interior pocked by hundreds of small lakes, its southern cliffs soaring 400 m.
features.look_for: Triangular island dotted with lakes

features.name: Landes forest
features.description: Western Europe's largest man-made forest: a million hectares of pines planted on drained sandy heath, sliced into a near-perfect grid of plots.
features.look_for: Vast dark forest cut in rectangular blocks

features.name: Harding Icefield
features.description: A 1,800 km2 relic of the ice age capping the Kenai Mountains, feeding nearly 40 glaciers. Only rock peaks called nunataks poke through its surface.
features.look_for: White ice cap with nunataks spilling glaciers to the sea

features.name: French Frigate Shoals
features.description: A crescent atoll with La Perouse Pinnacle, the last remnant of the old volcano. In 2018 a hurricane erased East Island entirely.
features.look_for: Crescent reef with a lone volcanic pinnacle in the open Pacific

features.name: Raiatea & Taha'a
features.description: Two mountainous volcanic islands sharing a single barrier reef and lagoon, forming a figure-eight outline. Raiatea's Taputapuatea marae was the religious centre of ancient Polynesia.
features.look_for: Two islands within one reef outline

features.name: Toquepala mine
features.description: A near-perfect terraced bowl of a copper pit in the southern Peruvian desert, its concentric benches spiraling down like an amphitheater; nearby cave walls hold 10,000-year-old paintings.
features.look_for: Terraced circular pit

features.name: Langebaan Lagoon
features.description: A long turquoise lagoon running parallel to the Atlantic coast, sheltered behind a peninsula; fossil footprints 117,000 years old were found on its shore.
features.look_for: Long turquoise lagoon

features.name: Shishapangma
features.description: The lowest of the fourteen 8,000-metre peaks (8,027 m), the only one wholly inside China, with long glaciers draining north onto the plateau. It was the last 8,000er climbed (1964).
features.look_for: Snow massif with glaciers flowing onto brown plateau

features.name: Meili Snow Mountains
features.description: A glaciated range between the Mekong and Salween crowned by sacred Kawagebo (6,740 m), which has never been climbed. Its Mingyong glacier descends to forest.
features.look_for: Sharp snowy ridge between deep gorges

features.name: Jade Dragon Snow Mountain
features.description: A sharp snow-capped ridge north of Lijiang towering 3,000 m above Tiger Leaping Gorge, the southernmost glaciers in Eurasia. Its glaciers are retreating fast.
features.look_for: Narrow snowy ridge above a deep gorge

features.name: Inglefield Land
features.description: A rare ice-free coastal plateau in Northwest Greenland, banded with bare rock between the ice sheet edge and the sea.
features.look_for: Bare brown coastal strip between ice sheet and sea

features.name: Columbia Glacier
features.description: One of the fastest-retreating glaciers in the world: its calving front has withdrawn about 20 km since 1980, leaving a new fjord behind.
features.look_for: Long ice tongue ending in an iceberg-filled fjord

features.name: Columbia Icefield
features.description: Meltwater from this icefield flows to three oceans (Pacific, Atlantic and Arctic). Its Athabasca Glacier tongue is reachable by road.
features.look_for: White ice cap astride the Rockies spilling glaciers in all directions

features.name: Big Bend Rio Grande Canyons
features.description: The Rio Grande cuts 450 m sheer gorges through the Mesa de Anguila; the river is the US-Mexico border here.
features.look_for: River slicing straight through a limestone wall

features.name: Little Missouri Badlands
features.description: Eroded layers of clay, sandstone and lignite coal (some burning underground) along the Little Missouri River.
features.look_for: Gullied banded badlands along a meandering river in the plains

features.name: Palmerston Atoll
features.description: A triangular ring of reef and islets around a turquoise lagoon, populated almost entirely by descendants of a single Englishman, William Marsters, who settled in 1863.
features.look_for: Triangular atoll with bright lagoon

features.name: Walvis Bay Lagoon and Salt Works
features.description: A lagoon sheltered behind the long Pelican Point spit, beside a grid of salt evaporation ponds in pink and green. One of southern Africa's richest wetland bird sites.
features.look_for: Lagoon, spit and salt ponds

features.name: Hingol National Park
features.description: Wind-carved mudstone badlands and the Hingol River gorge on the Makran coast, with natural sculptures like the 'Princess of Hope'. The Chandragup mud volcano lies within.
features.look_for: Banded eroded hills and a river gorge

features.name: Jameson Land
features.description: A broad, ice-free brown lowland north of Scoresby Sund's mouth, conspicuously smooth and bare next to the icy mountains around it.
features.look_for: Smooth bare brown lowland beside icy mountains

features.name: Médanos de Samalayuca
features.description: An isolated sea of quartz dunes in the Chihuahuan Desert, used as a filming location for desert scenes.
features.look_for: Pale yellow dune field in the Chihuahuan desert south of Ciudad Juárez

verified.note: pale dune triangle east of frame center; recentered

features.name: Si Phan Don
features.description: 'Four Thousand Islands': the Mekong spreads up to 14 km wide into a maze of channels and islands before thundering over the Khone Falls. Irrawaddy dolphins live in its pools.
features.look_for: River splits into maze of islands and channels

features.name: Mount Rinjani
features.description: A towering volcano on Lombok with a crescent-shaped crater lake, Segara Anak, from which a new cone (Barujari) rises. A huge eruption from nearby Samalas in 1257 shook global climate.
features.look_for: Caldera with crescent lake and inner cone

features.name: Kvarken Archipelago
features.description: Land rising 8 mm a year from post-glacial rebound produces an ever-growing maze of islands crossed by parallel De Geer moraine ridges.
features.look_for: Maze of islands with parallel ridges in shallow sea

features.name: Alqueva Reservoir
features.description: Western Europe's largest artificial lake, an extravagantly dendritic web of flooded valleys spreading across the Alentejo.
features.look_for: Huge many-branched reservoir in dry farmland

verified.note: dendritic arms visible but low contrast

features.name: Augustine Volcano
features.description: A whole island in Cook Inlet built by a single lava dome volcano, its flanks streaked with grey pyroclastic deposits. It erupted most recently in 2006.
features.look_for: Round island that is entirely one grey volcanic cone

features.name: Thelon Esker
features.description: The Barren Grounds are threaded by some of the longest eskers on Earth, gravel ridges left by rivers beneath the ice sheet; the Thelon esker runs for about 800 km.
features.look_for: Thin pale sinuous ridges crossing lake-studded tundra

verified.note: thin pale esker lines across lake country

features.name: Sierrita & Mission Mines
features.description: Copper mines near Green Valley whose pale tailings mesas cover tens of square kilometres, rivaling the natural landscape in scale.
features.look_for: Huge flat-topped grey tailings plateaus and pits south of Tucson

features.name: Lunar Crater Volcanic Field
features.description: Over 100 cinder cones and maars dot this field; NASA used it to train Apollo astronauts in recognizing lunar-like craters.
features.look_for: Black cinder cones and lava flows in a pale Nevada valley

features.name: Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta
features.description: An inland delta of 57 leveed islands, many now below sea level because their peat soils have oxidized away.
features.look_for: Maze of channels around sunken island farms

verified.note: wiki point near Suisun; recentered on delta

features.name: Land Between the Lakes
features.description: Kentucky Lake and Lake Barkley, dammed rivers just a few km apart, enclose a 70 km forested strip.
features.look_for: Long forested peninsula between two parallel dendritic reservoirs

features.name: Christmas Island
features.description: A steep-sided volcanic island in the Indian Ocean, mostly covered in rainforest with patches of phosphate mines. Its annual red crab migration involves tens of millions of crabs.
features.look_for: Green island with pale mine patches

features.name: Lake Ellesmere / Te Waihora
features.description: A large shallow lagoon south of Banks Peninsula separated from the sea by the long gravel Kaitorete Spit. It is a vital bird habitat.
features.look_for: Pale lagoon behind a long gravel spit

features.name: Malden Island
features.description: An uninhabited, arid triangular island with a pale-green interior of salt lagoons, mined for guano in the 1800s. Britain detonated its first H-bomb tests offshore in 1957.
features.look_for: Triangular pale island with greenish interior

features.name: Kapingamarangi
features.description: The southernmost atoll of Micronesia, a round reef ring with many small islets on its eastern side, inhabited by Polynesians. It lies only about 120 km north of the equator.
features.look_for: Round reef ring with islets on one side

features.name: Parinacota & Pomerape (Payachata)
features.description: Twin snow-capped cones on the Chile–Bolivia border; Parinacota's flank collapsed 8,000 years ago, damming Lago Chungará.
features.look_for: Pair of white-capped cones

features.name: Saemangeum
features.description: A 33.9 km seawall, the world's longest, enclosing a former tidal estuary that is being turned into new land. The straight dyke cuts across the sea like a ruler line.
features.look_for: Long straight seawall enclosing reclaimed flats

features.name: Hachirōgata
features.description: Once Japan's second-largest lake, drained in the 1960s into a near-perfect oval polder of rice fields with a canal ring. The new village of Ogata was built in its center.
features.look_for: Big oval of geometric rice fields ringed by water

features.name: Nordvestfjord
features.description: The longest arm of Scoresby Sund, a narrow canyon-fjord 2 km deep ending at Daugaard-Jensen Glacier, filled with icebergs.
features.look_for: Long narrow iceberg-filled arm of a fjord system

features.name: Owens Lake
features.description: Drained by the Los Angeles Aqueduct in the 1920s, it became the largest dust source in the US; shallow flooding cells now tint it in a mosaic of colors.
features.look_for: Dry lakebed patchworked with pink, green and white dust-control ponds

features.name: Lake of the Ozarks
features.description: Bagnell Dam flooded the meandering Osage River in 1931, giving the reservoir its dragon shape and more shoreline than the California coast.
features.look_for: Serpent-shaped reservoir with endless winding arms in forest

features.name: Lake Eildon
features.description: A large reservoir with a highly dendritic shoreline in Victoria's high country, its arms reaching into forested valleys. It is a major water source for northern Victoria's irrigation.
features.look_for: Many-armed reservoir in forested hills

features.name: Marakei
features.description: A Kiribati atoll whose ring of land is almost unbroken, enclosing a nearly landlocked lagoon tinted turquoise and green. Tradition holds that newcomers must make a ritual circuit of the island.
features.look_for: Almost-closed oval ring of land around a lagoon

features.name: Gran Bajo de San Julián
features.description: A deep wind-scoured depression in the Patagonian steppe holding Laguna del Carbón, at -105 m the lowest point in the Americas.
features.look_for: Pale salt floor in a sunken basin

features.name: Mount Unzen
features.description: A volcanic complex on the Shimabara peninsula whose 1991 pyroclastic flows killed 43 people; its new lava dome, Heisei-shinzan, is still bare. Its 1792 collapse caused Japan's worst volcanic disaster.
features.look_for: Volcano with grey scar of recent flows

features.name: Greater Tokyo
features.description: The world's largest metropolitan area, a continuous grey sprawl around Tokyo Bay, whose shores are almost entirely artificial reclaimed land. Home to some 37 million people.
features.look_for: Vast grey sprawl around a bay with geometric landfill

features.name: Kangchenjunga
features.description: The world's third-highest mountain (8,586 m), a massif of five summits with long glaciers spreading into Nepal and Sikkim. Climbers traditionally stop short of the summit out of respect.
features.look_for: Large snow massif with radiating glaciers

features.name: Kathmandu Valley
features.description: A bowl-shaped former lakebed filled with the grey sprawl of Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur, cupped by green hills. Legend says the bodhisattva Manjushri drained its lake with a sword.
features.look_for: Grey city blob filling a round valley

features.name: Herðubreið
features.description: The 'queen of Icelandic mountains': a flat-topped, steep-sided tuya formed by an eruption under an ice-age glacier.
features.look_for: Steep-sided flat-topped mountain alone in lava desert

features.name: Fucine Lake basin
features.description: Once Italy's third-largest lake, drained in 1878; its flat bed is now a striking oval grid of fields ringed by mountains.
features.look_for: Oval basin of straight-grid fields among mountains

verified.note: oval grid of fields in mountains, striking

features.name: Livanjsko Polje
features.description: One of the world's largest karst poljes: a flat basin 65 km long between bare limestone ridges, flooding seasonally.
features.look_for: Long flat basin floor between bare ridges

features.name: Bingham Canyon Mine
features.description: One of the deepest open-pit mines in the world, over 1.2 km deep and 4 km wide. It has produced more copper than any other mine in history.
features.look_for: Gigantic terraced spiral pit in the Oquirrh Mountains

features.name: Kata Tjuta
features.description: A cluster of 36 huge domed rock heads about 25 km west of Uluru, forming a knot of rounded shadows on the plain. Its tallest dome, Mount Olga, is about 200 m higher than Uluru.
features.look_for: Cluster of rounded domes with deep clefts

features.name: Kaipara Harbour
features.description: A sprawling, many-armed harbour on the North Island's west coast with an extensive tidal network. It is one of the largest harbours in the Southern Hemisphere.
features.look_for: Many-armed tidal harbour behind narrow entrance

features.name: Ninigo Islands
features.description: A remote cluster of atolls in the western Admiralty Islands of PNG, scattered loops of reef and tiny islets in deep blue water. Its communities run locally managed marine reserves.
features.look_for: Scattered small reef loops

features.name: Confluence of the Blue and White Nile
features.description: Where the blue-grey Blue Nile and the paler White Nile meet at Khartoum, their different-coloured waters flowing side by side for kilometres.
features.look_for: Two different-coloured rivers merging

features.name: Guilin-Yangshuo Karst
features.description: A forest of steep limestone tower peaks along the Li River, the dreamlike landscape of Chinese ink paintings. From above it looks like a field of green egg cartons.
features.look_for: Dense bumpy green karst towers along a river

verified.note: karst texture visible; better at z11+

features.name: Lunana Glacial Lakes
features.description: A remote Bhutanese valley at the foot of the Himalaya with a string of glacier-fed lakes, some of which have burst in deadly floods. Turquoise and grey meltwater lakes sit in front of glaciers.
features.look_for: Glacial lakes below snow peaks

features.name: Hambach lignite mine
features.description: Germany's deepest opencast pit (~400 m), next to the remnant Hambach Forest and the huge Sophienhöhe spoil hill.
features.look_for: Deep terraced brown pit beside a forested hill

features.name: El Malpais
features.description: Black basalt flows from the Zuni-Bandera field, some only 3,900 years old, filled this valley; their lava tubes host perennial ice caves.
features.look_for: Dark lava flows filling a valley with sandstone bluffs at the edge

features.name: Montebello Islands
features.description: A flat chain of over 100 limestone islands off the Pilbara where Britain tested atomic bombs in 1952 and 1956. Shallow turquoise lagoons wind between the islands.
features.look_for: Low island chain with turquoise lagoons

features.name: Johnston Atoll
features.description: A US atoll in the open Pacific, built up by dredging into an enlarged airstrip island inside a broad reef. It was a nuclear test and chemical weapons disposal site.
features.look_for: Broad reef shelf with rectangular island

features.name: Tasermiut Fjord
features.description: A 70 km fjord in South Greenland flanked by big-wall granite spires (Ketil, Ulamertorsuaq), with greener valleys near its mouth.
features.look_for: Narrow fjord between towering grey peaks

features.name: Ojos del Salado
features.description: The highest volcano on Earth (6,893 m), a pale massif of craters and snow patches on the Chile–Argentina border with a tiny crater lake near its summit.
features.look_for: Pale massif with scattered snow

features.name: Ronne-Filchner Ice Shelf
features.description: The second-largest ice shelf on Earth, a vast flat plate filling the southern Weddell Sea.
features.look_for: Vast flat ice

verified.note: not image-checked: Natural Earth geometry / continental-scale feature

features.name: Qiandao Lake
features.description: A man-made lake with 1,078 islands (the drowned hilltops of a valley flooded in 1959), its intricate shoreline like a maze. Two ancient cities lie beneath its water.
features.look_for: Labyrinth of green islands in blue water

features.name: Aso Caldera
features.description: One of the largest calderas in the world (25 x 18 km), its floor filled with rice fields and towns around active Nakadake crater. Grassy rims stand out from surrounding forest.
features.look_for: Huge oval basin of farmland with central volcanic cones

features.name: Baltoro Glacier
features.description: A 63 km river of ice striped with dark medial moraines, flowing past four 8,000 m peaks including K2. Concordia, its confluence, is called the 'throne room of the mountain gods'.
features.look_for: Long glacier with dark stripes

features.name: Tonle Sap Floodplain
features.description: Each monsoon the Mekong forces the Tonle Sap river to reverse and the lake swells fivefold, flooding a ring of forest and fields. Floating villages follow the shoreline.
features.look_for: Huge lake surrounded by flooded forest ring

features.name: Lakes Ohrid & Prespa
features.description: Twin tectonic lakes separated by a mountain ridge; Ohrid is one of the oldest lakes on Earth, over a million years old.
features.look_for: Two large lakes side by side separated by a ridge

features.name: Breiðafjörður
features.description: A broad bay between the Westfjords and Snæfellsnes strewn with thousands of tiny islands and skerries.
features.look_for: Wide bay sprinkled with countless small islets

features.name: Ward Hunt Ice Shelf
features.description: Formerly the largest ice shelf in the Arctic, its surface is corrugated into parallel meltwater ridges. It has fractured repeatedly since 2000.
features.look_for: Ribbed floating ice shelf along Ellesmere's north coast

features.name: Belcher Islands
features.description: An archipelago in Hudson Bay whose islands are the exposed crests of tightly folded 2-billion-year-old strata, giving them strange curled, fishhook shapes.
features.look_for: Swirling hook-shaped islands traced by folded rock layers

features.name: Shiprock and its Dikes
features.description: The eroded throat of a volcano rising 480 m above the plain, with dark volcanic dikes running for kilometres like walls in three directions.
features.look_for: Dark rock spire with long straight black walls radiating across the desert

features.name: Swain Reefs
features.description: A vast field of hundreds of small reefs at the southern end of the Great Barrier Reef, nearly 250 km offshore. They form a speckled triangle in deep blue water.
features.look_for: Dense speckled reef field in the open sea

features.name: Mount Ruapehu
features.description: The North Island's highest peak, a 2,797 m active stratovolcano with a snowcap and summit crater lake. It erupted in 1995-96 and caused the 1953 Tangiwai rail disaster via a lahar.
features.look_for: Snowy cone in brown volcanic plateau

features.name: Rangitoto Island
features.description: A young symmetrical shield volcano in Auckland's harbour, formed about 600 years ago, covered in dark pohutukawa forest. It is Auckland's youngest and largest volcano.
features.look_for: Round dark island with central cone

features.name: Swartberg Range
features.description: Long parallel ridges of the Cape Fold Belt in the Western Cape, crumpled like a rug pushed against a wall, with zigzag passes cutting through them.
features.look_for: Parallel folded ridges

features.name: Dead Sea Evaporation Ponds
features.description: The southern basin of the Dead Sea is now a grid of turquoise evaporation ponds for potash and salt, separated by dikes from the shrinking northern basin.
features.look_for: Turquoise rectangular ponds

features.name: Muztagh Ata
features.description: A broad glaciated dome (7,546 m) at the eastern edge of the Pamirs with radiating glaciers, beside turquoise Karakul Lake. Its gentle slopes make it a popular ski-mountaineering peak.
features.look_for: Big white dome with radiating glacier tongues

features.name: Sermilik Fjord
features.description: A long fjord near Tasiilaq perpetually full of icebergs shed by Helheim Glacier, a white-speckled channel through dark coastal mountains.
features.look_for: Fjord speckled with countless icebergs

features.name: Hinlopen Strait
features.description: The strait between Spitsbergen and Nordaustlandet, lined with ice cliffs and dotted with small islands; often choked with drift ice.
features.look_for: Narrow strait between two icy islands

features.name: Noordoostpolder
features.description: A 1942 polder with a radial-and-grid field pattern converging on the town of Emmeloord; its tulip fields stripe it with colour in spring.
features.look_for: Radial grid of reclaimed fields

features.name: North Keeling
features.description: A tiny isolated atoll north of the main Cocos group, a ring of land almost enclosing a dark lagoon. It is a seabird sanctuary within Pulu Keeling National Park.
features.look_for: Small ring island around dark lagoon

features.name: Rossel Lagoon
features.description: A huge lagoon at the end of the Louisiade Archipelago, with Rossel Island inside it and a reef fringing the deep sea. Its people speak Yele, a language isolate.
features.look_for: Long reef with island in turquoise lagoon

features.name: Fakaofo
features.description: A Tokelau atoll whose narrow reef ring frames a lagoon criss-crossed by coral ridges like veins. Its tiny village islet of Fale is one of the most densely packed places in the Pacific.
features.look_for: Reef ring with lacy coral ridges in the lagoon

features.name: White Desert
features.description: A white chalk plain studded with wind-carved mushroom-shaped rock formations north of Farafra. Seen from above, chalk patches glow against orange sand.
features.look_for: Bright white chalk patches

features.name: Sayram Lake
features.description: A deep blue alpine lake in a bowl of the Borohoro Shan, ringed by green pasture and dark spruce. Locals call it 'the last tear of the Atlantic' as it is the furthest point reached by Atlantic moisture.
features.look_for: Oval deep-blue lake in green mountains

features.name: Tengger Desert
features.description: A sea of yellow dunes along the Yellow River dotted with small lakes, now bordered by vast solar farms. Some solar panels near Zhongwei are arranged in the shape of a galloping horse.
features.look_for: Yellow dune sea with dark solar-panel blocks

features.name: Fiery Cross Reef
features.description: A submerged reef turned into an artificial island airbase with a 3 km runway in the Spratlys, one of the largest reclamation projects in the South China Sea.
features.look_for: Long artificial island with runway in sea

features.name: Eyjafjallajökull
features.description: A small ice-capped volcano whose 2010 ash cloud shut down European air traffic for days; its summit crater shows through the ice.
features.look_for: Small round ice cap with a summit crater

features.name: Białowieża Forest
features.description: Europe's last primeval lowland forest, a dark green block sharply bounded by farmland, home of the wild bison.
features.look_for: Big dark forest block with crisp edges

features.name: Imperial Valley Fields
features.description: Irrigated by the All-American Canal, this below-sea-level desert valley is a sharp-edged grid of crops, ending abruptly at bare sand.
features.look_for: Dense green checkerboard of fields in a pure desert basin

verified.note: green field grid south of Salton Sea

features.name: Lake Mungo
features.description: A dry lake bed with a bright crescent dune (the Walls of China) along its eastern shore in the Willandra Lakes. Mungo Man and Mungo Lady, found here, are around 40,000 years old.
features.look_for: Grey dry lake with a bright white crescent dune

features.name: Loy Yang mine
features.description: A vast brown-coal open cut in the Latrobe Valley, its terraced pit and conveyor lines dominating the farmland. It feeds the largest power station in Victoria.
features.look_for: Huge stepped brown pit in green farmland

features.name: Volga-Akhtuba Floodplain
features.description: A green ribbon of channels, oxbows and meadows between the Volga and its distributary Akhtuba, a vivid strip cutting through dry brown steppe.
features.look_for: Green braided strip in brown semi-desert

verified.note: green strip visible in brown steppe

features.name: Deception Island
features.description: A ring-shaped island that is the flooded caldera of an active volcano; ships sail into its central bay through a narrow gap called Neptune's Bellows.
features.look_for: Ring island with flooded center

features.name: Nevado Sajama
features.description: Bolivia's highest peak (6,542 m), an isolated ice-capped cone on the Altiplano ringed by the world's highest-elevation forest of queñua trees.
features.look_for: Lone white-capped cone on brown plateau

verified.note: isolated white cone on brown plateau

features.name: Minya Konka
features.description: Sichuan's highest peak (7,556 m), a pyramid of ice with glaciers descending into forest east of the Tibetan plateau. Its Hailuogou glacier reaches down to 2,850 m.
features.look_for: Snow massif with long glaciers into green forest

features.name: Singrauli Coalfield
features.description: Dozens of open-pit coal mines and power plants, India's 'energy capital', creating dark terraced scars and grey ash ponds. It generates a large share of India's coal power.
features.look_for: Dark terraced pits and grey ponds

features.name: Cà Mau Peninsula
features.description: The southern tip of Vietnam, a mangrove-fringed point growing into the sea, with a dense grid of shrimp ponds inland. Mud deposits extend it up to 100 m per year.
features.look_for: Triangular point with grid of ponds and mangroves

features.name: Faroe Islands
features.description: Eighteen steep, treeless volcanic islands arranged like shards in the North Atlantic, slashed by narrow sounds and fjords.
features.look_for: Cluster of steep green-brown islands cut by narrow channels

features.name: Sierra Nevada (Spain)
features.description: Mainland Spain's highest range (Mulhacén, 3,479 m), a snowcapped ridge visible from the Mediterranean coast.
features.look_for: Snow-capped ridge in dry country

features.name: Algodones Dunes
features.description: California's largest dune field, a 70 km ribbon of sand that the All-American Canal and Interstate 8 must cross. Star Wars filmed scenes here.
features.look_for: Long narrow band of golden dunes cutting through flat desert

features.name: Mississippi Bird's-foot Delta
features.description: The modern delta has built long levee-lined fingers like a bird's foot out onto the continental shelf; it is sinking and eroding fast.
features.look_for: Thin claw-like fingers of land reaching into the Gulf

features.name: Copper Canyon
features.description: Six canyons that together are larger and in parts deeper than the Grand Canyon, cut into the Sierra Madre Occidental.
features.look_for: Network of deep green-shadowed gorges cutting the Sierra Madre plateau

verified.note: rugged canyon texture; less striking than expected

features.name: Georgia Sea Island Marshes
features.description: Georgia's coast holds a third of the remaining salt marsh on the US Atlantic coast, a maze of tidal creeks behind the Sea Islands.
features.look_for: Barrier islands backed by vast tan salt marshes threaded by channels

features.name: West Baray and Angkor
features.description: An 8 km x 2 km rectangular reservoir built by the Khmer Empire around 1050, next to the moated square of Angkor Wat. The Angkor complex's geometry is clear from above.
features.look_for: Large water rectangle and moated squares in forest

features.name: Mount Tambora
features.description: A 6 km-wide, 1 km-deep caldera left by the largest eruption in recorded history (1815), which caused the 'Year Without a Summer' in 1816. It sits on its own peninsula of Sumbawa.
features.look_for: Big deep caldera on a round peninsula

features.name: Mutsu Bay and Shimokita
features.description: The axe-shaped Shimokita Peninsula wraps around Mutsu Bay at the north tip of Honshu. Osorezan volcano, believed to be a gateway to the afterlife, sits in its 'blade'.
features.look_for: Axe-shaped peninsula around a round bay

features.name: Caldera de Taburiente
features.description: A huge erosional crater 8 km across on La Palma, walls up to 2,000 m high, drained by a single gorge.
features.look_for: Big forested amphitheatre with one outlet gorge

features.name: Mount St. Helens
features.description: The 1980 lateral blast removed 400 m of summit and flattened 600 km2 of forest; the grey pumice plain and Spirit Lake log mats are still obvious.
features.look_for: Horseshoe crater opening north onto a grey blast zone

features.name: Labrador Trough Iron Mines
features.description: The Mont-Wright and Labrador City/Wabush mines strip iron ore from the Labrador Trough, creating rust-colored scars in the boreal forest.
features.look_for: Huge red-grey pits and tailings among blue lakes and taiga

features.name: Lake Hopkins
features.description: A small salt lake in the Gibson Desert crowded with round dark islands, looking like a sheet of white lace or a sponge from above. It lies in remote Ngaanyatjarra lands.
features.look_for: White salt pan full of dark rounded islands

features.name: Tahiti
features.description: A figure-eight volcanic island: the large round Tahiti Nui joined to smaller Tahiti Iti by the Taravao isthmus, with deep radial valleys. It is the largest island of French Polynesia.
features.look_for: Figure-eight island with radial valleys

features.name: Niau
features.description: A raised atoll with a completely closed lagoon, so isolated from the sea that it has turned a dark green-brown colour. It is the last home of the critically endangered Tuamotu kingfisher.
features.look_for: Dark closed lagoon inside a green rim

features.name: Nemrut Caldera
features.description: A 7 km caldera on the shore of Lake Van, half filled by a deep, cold, dark-blue crescent lake next to a smaller warm lake. One of the largest calderas in Turkey.
features.look_for: Caldera holding a dark crescent lake

features.name: Meghna Estuary
features.description: A huge estuary of shifting sandy islands (chars) and muddy water where the combined Ganges and Brahmaputra reach the sea. Bhola, the largest island, is regularly struck by cyclones.
features.look_for: Large muddy estuary with shifting islands

features.name: Ha Long Bay
features.description: About 1,600 limestone karst islands and islets rise from emerald water, the drowned tops of a karst landscape. Together with Lan Ha Bay it forms one of the world's great seascapes.
features.look_for: Sea dotted with countless small green islets

features.name: Kongsfjorden
features.description: A glacier-fringed fjord on Spitsbergen ending in tidewater fronts of Kongsbreen; Ny-Ålesund, the northernmost settlement, sits on its shore.
features.look_for: Fjord ending at white glacier fronts

features.name: Maasvlakte
features.description: Land reclaimed from the North Sea for the Port of Rotterdam, a geometric spit of docks and container terminals poking into the sea.
features.look_for: Geometric artificial land jutting into the sea

features.name: Deliblato Sands
features.description: Europe's largest continental sand area, an elliptical patch of stabilized dunes on the Pannonian plain.
features.look_for: Oval patch of rough wooded sand amid fields

verified.note: dark oval of wooded sand distinct

features.name: Wind River Range Glaciers
features.description: The Wind River Range holds the largest glaciers in the US Rockies, including Gannett Glacier on Gannett Peak.
features.look_for: Granite crest with white glacier patches and many cirque lakes

features.name: Mauna Loa
features.description: The largest active volcano on Earth by volume, rising 9 km from the sea floor; dark flows spread in all directions from its Moku'āweoweo caldera.
features.look_for: Immense gentle dome scored by dark lava flows radiating from the summit

features.name: Laguna de Términos
features.description: The largest coastal lagoon in Mexico, separated from the Gulf by Isla del Carmen; tidal plumes swirl through its two inlets.
features.look_for: Large brown lagoon behind a barrier island with sediment plumes

features.name: Suwarrow
features.description: An uninhabited Cook Islands atoll and national park, a pale reef ring dotted with tiny motu. New Zealander Tom Neale lived here alone for years and wrote "An Island to Oneself".
features.look_for: Irregular reef ring with tiny islets

features.name: Nuku Hiva
features.description: The largest of the Marquesas Islands, a rugged eroded volcano with steep cliffs and the deep bay of Taiohae, a drowned caldera. Herman Melville based his novel Typee on time spent here.
features.look_for: Rugged island with deep bays

features.name: Teraina
features.description: A raised coral island with no lagoon but a large freshwater lake and peat bogs in its centre, among the very few in the open Pacific. It looks like a dark-eyed oval in the sea.
features.look_for: Oval island with dark central lake

features.name: Pagan
features.description: A volcanic island in the Northern Marianas, made of two volcanoes joined by a narrow isthmus with two lakes. Its 1981 eruption forced the evacuation of its residents.
features.look_for: Two volcanic lobes joined by a narrow neck

features.name: Maipo & Diamante caldera
features.description: A perfect cone sitting inside the 20 km Diamante caldera, with blue Laguna del Diamante at its foot.
features.look_for: Cone in oval caldera next to blue lake

verified.note: white-streaked cone in dark caldera beside black lake

features.name: Timanfaya Lava Fields
features.description: A black, cratered landscape of lava fields on Lanzarote from the 1730-36 eruptions, which buried villages; the ground is still hot enough to roast food.
features.look_for: Dark lava fields

features.name: Mount Pinatubo
features.description: Its 1991 eruption, the second-largest of the 20th century, left a 2.5 km caldera lake and vast grey lahar valleys radiating across Luzon. It cooled the globe by 0.5 C.
features.look_for: Crater lake with grey ash valleys radiating out

features.name: Garzweiler lignite mine
features.description: A vast tan opencast pit 11 km long, swallowing villages; giant bucket-wheel excavators work its terraced walls.
features.look_for: Enormous tan terraced pit in farmland

features.name: Iron Gates
features.description: The Danube squeezes through a 134 km gorge in the Carpathians, at Kazan only 150 m wide, now dammed into a long lake.
features.look_for: River narrowing through a forested mountain gorge

features.name: Barnes Ice Cap
features.description: The last remnant of the Laurentide Ice Sheet that covered much of North America; it contains ice more than 20,000 years old and is shrinking fast.
features.look_for: Elongated white ice dome in the brown middle of Baffin Island

features.name: Sam Ford Fjord
features.description: Baffin's east coast is cut by fjords with some of the tallest sea cliffs on Earth; Sam Ford Fjord's walls rise more than 1,000 m straight from the water.
features.look_for: Deep fjords lined by sheer granite walls on Baffin Island

verified.note: ice and fjords of NE Baffin

features.name: Milford Sound
features.description: A fiord carved by glaciers in Fiordland, 15 km long, with steep cliffs and Mitre Peak rising 1,692 m. It is one of the wettest inhabited places on Earth.
features.look_for: Narrow dark fiord between steep peaks

features.name: Mount Aspiring / Tititea
features.description: A pyramid-shaped peak of 3,033 m surrounded by glaciers, called the Matterhorn of the South. It is the highest peak outside the Aoraki area.
features.look_for: Snowy pyramid peak with glaciers

features.name: Plaine des Lacs & Goro nickel
features.description: A red-earth landscape of nickel laterite in southern New Caledonia, scattered with lakes and mines. The red soils are among the most striking on Earth.
features.look_for: Red bare earth with lakes

features.name: Tabuaeran
features.description: A Kiribati atoll whose lagoon is netted with an intricate web of white coral ridges and turquoise pools. It was a relay station on the 1902 trans-Pacific telegraph cable.
features.look_for: Bean-shaped atoll with lacy lagoon

features.name: Bin el Ouidane Reservoir
features.description: A twisting blue reservoir drowned into a Middle Atlas valley, its arms snaking between rumpled ridges. It is one of Morocco's largest dams.
features.look_for: Blue reservoir in folded mountains

features.name: Jebel Uweinat
features.description: A ring-shaped granite massif where Egypt, Libya and Sudan meet, rising almost 2,000 m out of the Sahara. Its caves hold prehistoric paintings.
features.look_for: Dark ring massif in the tri-border desert

features.name: East Oweinat Project
features.description: A huge block of center-pivot farms in Egypt's remotest desert near Gebel Uweinat, laid out in dense rectangular grids. It looks like circuit board traced on sand.
features.look_for: Dense grid of pivot circles

features.name: Qattara Depression
features.description: A 300 km basin dropping to 133 m below sea level in Egypt's Western Desert, floored with salt marsh and sabkha. It blocked tank movements at El Alamein in WWII.
features.look_for: Huge pale basin edged by cliffs

features.name: Sossusvlei
features.description: A dead-end clay pan where the Tsauchab River dies among giant red star dunes, forming a white tongue in the red sand. Nearby Deadvlei holds 900-year-old dead camelthorn trees.
features.look_for: White clay pan in red dunes

features.name: Songkhla Lake
features.description: Thailand's largest lake, a lagoon complex running parallel to the Gulf of Thailand coast, with a freshwater upper section and brackish lower part. Its colors grade from green to brown.
features.look_for: Long lagoon behind a sand barrier

features.name: North Frisian Islands & Halligen
features.description: Sylt, Amrum, Föhr and the tiny undiked Halligen sit in a sea of tidal flats and channels.
features.look_for: Islands and flats in a muddy tidal sea

features.name: Salin-de-Giraud salt pans
features.description: Europe's largest salt works, a patchwork of evaporation ponds in vivid pinks, reds and turquoise from salt-loving algae.
features.look_for: Patchwork of pink, red and blue ponds

features.name: Great Brăila Island
features.description: The Danube splits into two arms around a 60 km island polder, now a geometric grid of fields with wetlands at its edges.
features.look_for: Long river island with two Danube arms

features.name: Prince Charles Island
features.description: A 9,500 km2 island so low and flat that it was not noticed by Europeans until an aerial survey in 1948, despite being larger than Cyprus.
features.look_for: Pale flat island in Foxe Basin with ringed beach ridges

features.name: Great Bahama Bank
features.description: A carbonate platform under only a few metres of water, glowing turquoise against the deep ocean; the Tongue of the Ocean, a 2 km deep trench, cuts into it.
features.look_for: Immense luminous turquoise shoal around a deep blue abyss

features.name: Anticosti Island
features.description: A 220 km limestone island in the Gulf of St. Lawrence, whose shores expose some of the best fossil records of the end-Ordovician extinction.
features.look_for: Long flat island with striped limestone ledges and wide tidal platforms

features.name: Berkeley Pit
features.description: A former copper pit, 540 m deep, slowly filling with acidic, metal-laden water; in 2016 thousands of snow geese died after landing on it.
features.look_for: Big pit filled with rust-and-teal toxic water at the edge of Butte

features.name: Chirkey Reservoir
features.description: A vivid turquoise reservoir filling a twisting canyon of the Sulak River in the bare mountains of Dagestan. Its dam is one of the tallest arch dams in Russia.
features.look_for: Bright turquoise branching water in tan mountains

features.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
features.description: The largest ice-free region of Antarctica: bare brown valleys where katabatic winds sweep away all snow, the closest Earth analog to Mars.
features.look_for: Brown bare valleys among white ice

features.name: Byrd Glacier
features.description: A fast ice stream squeezing through a 25 km gap in the Transantarctic Mountains, its surface combed into long flow stripes as it pours into the Ross Ice Shelf.
features.look_for: Streaked glacier in a gap

features.name: Great Sand Sea
features.description: A vast field of long parallel dunes covering 72,000 km² between Egypt and Libya. Libyan Desert Glass, made by an ancient airburst, is scattered among its corridors.
features.look_for: Long pale sand ridges

features.name: Sakurajima
features.description: One of the world's most active volcanoes, erupting ash almost daily inside Kagoshima Bay, which is itself the flooded Aira caldera. A 1914 lava flow joined the former island to the mainland.
features.look_for: Grey ashy volcanic island in a bay

features.name: Mũi Né Dunes
features.description: White and red sand dunes on the coast of Binh Thuan, unusual in tropical Vietnam, with small lakes between them. The red dunes are colored by iron oxide.
features.look_for: Pale and red dune patches by the sea

verified.note: white and red dunes strikingly clear

features.name: Taal Volcano
features.description: A lake in a caldera with a volcanic island inside, which itself has a crater lake - a lake within an island within a lake within an island. It erupted violently in 2020.
features.look_for: Big lake with central island volcano

features.name: Stauning Alps
features.description: A jagged alpine range packed with glaciers between Scoresby Sund and Kong Oscar Fjord, a dense web of ice-filled valleys.
features.look_for: Dense web of glaciers among sharp dark peaks

features.name: Grenen & Råbjerg Mile
features.description: Denmark's sharp northern point where two seas meet in a visible line; nearby Råbjerg Mile, a migrating dune, crawls 15 m a year.
features.look_for: Sharp sandy point with a pale dune patch

features.name: High Tatras
features.description: A compact, steep granite range with tarns and snow, rising abruptly out of flat basins - the Carpathians' only alpine peaks.
features.look_for: Compact rocky snowy range rising from lowland

features.name: Margherita di Savoia salt pans
features.description: Italy's largest salt works, a long strip of pink, green and white evaporation ponds along the Apulian coast.
features.look_for: Long coastal strip of coloured ponds

features.name: Penny Ice Cap
features.description: A 6,000 km2 ice cap in Auyuittuq National Park, feeding valley glaciers that drain into the dramatic fjords of eastern Baffin Island.
features.look_for: White ice cap on the Cumberland Peninsula with glaciers flowing to fjords

features.name: San Rafael Swell
features.description: A huge kidney-shaped anticline about 120 km long whose eroded rim, the San Rafael Reef, forms a sawtooth wall of tilted sandstone.
features.look_for: Giant oval dome of uplifted rock ringed by a jagged reef

features.name: Lake Lefroy
features.description: A brilliant white salt lake near Kambalda, crossed by causeways and mine haul roads. It is used for land sailing and gold and nickel mining extends right onto the lake bed.
features.look_for: Brilliant white lake with dark mine features

features.name: Century mine
features.description: A deep open pit with a flooded blue-green floor in the Gulf Country savanna, once one of the world's largest zinc mines. Tailings are now being reprocessed.
features.look_for: Dark pit lake and pale tailings dams in grey bush

features.name: Freycinet Peninsula
features.description: A granite peninsula on Tasmania's east coast with pink-orange granite peaks and the perfect arc of Wineglass Bay. Schouten Island lies just off its tip.
features.look_for: Pink granite peninsula with curved bays

features.name: Porgera mine
features.description: A gold mine high in the PNG highlands with grey terraced pits and dumps sprawling across the green ridges. It is one of the world's largest gold mines.
features.look_for: Grey mine scar sprawling across green ridges

features.name: Ducie Island
features.description: A tiny atoll at the eastern end of the Pitcairn Islands with a vivid blue lagoon inside a ring of pale coral rubble. It is one of the most remote atolls on Earth.
features.look_for: Small bright atoll with blue lagoon

features.name: Maloelap Atoll
features.description: A broad Marshallese atoll whose islet of Taroa still holds a wrecked Japanese WWII airbase. Its long reef rim encloses a deep lagoon with scattered patch reefs.
features.look_for: Large atoll ring with patch reefs

features.name: Ukok Plateau
features.description: A high, cold, lake-dotted plateau where Russia, China, Kazakhstan and Mongolia meet, famous for the 'Ice Maiden' frozen Pazyryk burial.
features.look_for: High bare plateau with small lakes and glaciers

verified.note: snowy peaks and lakes; plateau not sharply bounded

features.name: Japanese Alps
features.description: Japan's Northern Alps, the steepest range in the country, with cirques and small glaciers confirmed in 2012, the first known in Japan. Snow lingers into July.
features.look_for: Snowy rugged ridges in central Honshu

features.name: Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar
features.description: A large reservoir in the hills of the Singrauli coalfield, ringed by thermal power plants and huge open-pit coal mines. Fly ash ponds line its shores.
features.look_for: Branching reservoir among dark coal mines

features.name: Monywa Copper Mines
features.description: Open-pit copper mines and leach pads beside the Chindwin River, including the contested Letpadaung and Sabetaung pits. Bright blue-green ponds dot the site.
features.look_for: Grey pits with blue-green ponds near a river

features.name: Krakatoa
features.description: The remnants of the volcano that exploded in 1883: a ring of islands around a caldera with Anak Krakatau, 'child of Krakatoa', rising in the middle. Its 2018 collapse caused a deadly tsunami.
features.look_for: Ring of islands with dark central cone

features.name: Oosterschelde & Delta Works
features.description: Zeeland's drowned estuaries, sealed by a storm surge barrier 9 km long; the islands and tidal flats form a jigsaw.
features.look_for: Island jigsaw with dams across estuary mouths

features.name: Wood-Tikchik Lakes
features.description: Two chains of long glacially carved finger lakes, draining in steps to Bristol Bay. It is the largest state park in the United States.
features.look_for: Chain of long, deep finger lakes reaching into mountains

features.name: Cypress Hills
features.description: The highest point between the Rockies and Labrador; its plateau top escaped glaciation and is capped with lodgepole pine, an island of forest in the grasslands.
features.look_for: Dark forested plateau rising out of prairie

features.name: Haleakalā Crater
features.description: The "crater" of Haleakalā is actually an erosional valley 11 km long, its floor a Mars-like field of colorful cinder cones.
features.look_for: Huge red and black erosional crater with cinder cones on its floor

features.name: Cockpit Country
features.description: Polygonal karst where thousands of steep-sided "cockpit" depressions pack together like an egg carton; the area is so rugged it sheltered escaped Maroons.
features.look_for: Egg-carton forest of countless round sinkholes and hills

features.name: Great Plain of the Koukdjuak
features.description: A low plain on western Baffin Island hosting the world's largest goose colony, mostly lesser snow geese.
features.look_for: Flat pond-speckled tundra plain with tidal flats on Foxe Basin

features.name: Cambridge Gulf
features.description: A funnel-shaped gulf at Wyndham whose branching tidal creeks and vast mudflats form a pale dendritic pattern; five rivers drain into it. Tides here exceed 7 m.
features.look_for: Tree-like pale tidal channels at a gulf head

features.name: Uluru
features.description: A lone sandstone monolith 3.6 km long rising 348 m above the red dune plains, its dark fluted flanks casting long shadows. It is sacred to the Anangu people and the iconic heart of Australia.
features.look_for: Lone oval rock in red sand

features.name: Lord Howe Island
features.description: A crescent-shaped volcanic island with a turquoise reef lagoon and the twin peaks of Mount Lidgbird and Mount Gower. It has the world's southernmost coral reef.
features.look_for: Crescent island with turquoise lagoon

features.name: Kolombangara
features.description: A nearly perfectly round volcanic island 30 km across with streams radiating from its central peak. Dozens of streams radiate from its summit like spokes.
features.look_for: Perfect green circle island with radial streams

features.name: Maupiti
features.description: A small sister of Bora Bora: a craggy volcanic island inside a reef ring of long motu and a shallow turquoise lagoon. Its narrow pass is one of the trickiest in Polynesia.
features.look_for: Small island inside turquoise reef ring

features.name: Lake Baskunchak
features.description: A brilliant white salt lake in the brown Caspian steppe, so pure (99% NaCl) it has supplied much of Russia's table salt. Next to it rises Big Bogdo, a sacred hill.
features.look_for: Bright white oval in brown steppe

features.name: Chuquicamata
features.description: One of the largest open-pit mines on Earth: a terraced oval hole 4.3 km long and over 1 km deep in the Atacama, with a huge grey tailings field to the south.
features.look_for: Giant terraced oval pit and waste dumps

features.name: Nyungwe Forest
features.description: A block of montane rainforest in Rwanda with a strikingly sharp edge against densely farmed hills — a dark green island surrounded by cultivated land.
features.look_for: Dark forest block with sharp edge

features.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
features.description: Africa's highest mountain (5,895 m), a free-standing volcano with a snowy crater and a dark forest ring sharply framing it against the savanna.
features.look_for: Huge volcano with snow and forest ring

features.name: Kuiseb River Dune Barrier
features.description: A dry riverbed that the great Namib dune sea cannot cross: red dunes stop dead along its southern bank while bare grey gravel plains stretch away to the north.
features.look_for: Sharp dune boundary along a river

features.name: Ebinur Lake
features.description: A shrinking salt lake in the Dzungarian lowlands surrounded by bright white salt flats and wind-blown dust plumes. It is the source of frequent salt-dust storms in northern Xinjiang.
features.look_for: Shallow lake rimmed by white salt flats

features.name: Sambhar Salt Lake
features.description: India's largest inland salt lake, a shallow seasonal wetland split by a dam with rectangular pink and white salt pans on its eastern end. Flamingos winter here.
features.look_for: Pale shallow lake with grid of pink pans

features.name: Stockholm Archipelago
features.description: A scatter of some 30,000 rocky islands and skerries fanning out east of Stockholm.
features.look_for: Dense spray of small islands

verified.note: archipelago east of Stockholm; recentred after spot check

features.name: Lewis lochan country
features.description: The peat moorland of the Isle of Lewis is shattered into thousands of small lochans - more water than land in places.
features.look_for: Brown moor riddled with countless small lakes

features.name: Bylot Island
features.description: A mountainous, ice-capped island off northern Baffin, with valley glaciers spilling out on all sides. It is a major nesting area for greater snow geese.
features.look_for: Island almost entirely covered by ice and radiating glaciers

features.name: Hull–Rust–Mahoning Mine
features.description: Known as the "Grand Canyon of the North", the world's largest open-pit iron mine, over 5 km long.
features.look_for: Long terraced red-brown pit on the edge of Hibbing

features.name: Anaa
features.description: A Tuamotu atoll whose lagoon is almost completely enclosed, giving it an extraordinarily bright milky-turquoise colour visible from far away. It was devastated by a cyclone in 1906.
features.look_for: Glowing milky-turquoise enclosed lagoon

features.name: Rano Kau
features.description: A 1.6 km-wide extinct volcanic crater at the southwest tip of Easter Island, its floor filled with a lake covered in floating reed mats. The ceremonial village of Orongo sits on its rim.
features.look_for: Dark round crater on the island tip

features.name: Jaluit Atoll
features.description: A large atoll with a broad lagoon and over 90 islets on a long rim, the former German and Japanese administrative capital of the Marshalls. It is now a marine conservation area.
features.look_for: Large elongated atoll ring

features.name: Ebon Atoll
features.description: The southernmost atoll of the Marshall Islands, a nearly round ring with a lagoon and a pass on its western side. The first Christian mission in the Marshalls was established here in 1857.
features.look_for: Round reef ring

features.name: Salar de Arizaro
features.description: A long 1,600 km² salt flat in the Argentine Puna, framed by dark volcanoes; the black cone of Cono de Arita stands alone on its white surface.
features.look_for: Elongated white pan, tiny dark cone in the south

features.name: Cerro Galán caldera
features.description: One of the largest exposed calderas on Earth, a 35 km oval rim of pale ignimbrite with a resurgent dome and Laguna Diamante inside.
features.look_for: Giant oval ring of pale rock

verified.note: caldera rim subtle; Laguna Diamante visible

features.name: Kufra Center-Pivot Fields
features.description: Hundreds of dark-green center-pivot fields in the Libyan Sahara, watered from an ancient aquifer. They look like a pegboard of green dots on orange sand.
features.look_for: Grid of green circles in desert

features.name: Gross Brukkaros
features.description: An isolated extinct volcano in southern Namibia whose 2 km summit crater is surrounded by radial gullies, making it look like a giant starburst on the plain.
features.look_for: Crater with radial gullies

features.name: Ilha dos Tigres
features.description: A long, curving sand island off southern Angola that was a peninsula until the sea broke through its neck in 1962, stranding the fishing town of São Martinho dos Tigres.
features.look_for: Long sandy island

features.name: Cape Peninsula
features.description: A rocky peninsula curving south to the Cape of Good Hope, with Cape Town and Table Mountain at its northern end and False Bay to the east.
features.look_for: Narrow peninsula south of a city

features.name: Rub' al Khali Megadunes (Uruq al Mutaridah)
features.description: Giant crescent megadunes up to 250 m high, arranged in a regular lattice with pale salt flats in the hollows between them.
features.look_for: Regular lattice of huge dunes

features.name: Izu Ōshima
features.description: A volcanic island whose central caldera holds the black ash cone of Mihara, which erupted in 1986 forcing evacuation of the whole island. The ash desert is visible as a dark patch.
features.look_for: Island with dark summit caldera

features.name: Kosi Megafan
features.description: The Kosi, 'Sorrow of Bihar', has swept across a fan of sand 150 km wide as it shifted 120 km westward over two centuries. Its braided channels and pale sand scars stand out on the plain.
features.look_for: Fan of braided sandy channels on the plain

features.name: Wakhan Corridor
features.description: A narrow strip of Afghanistan between Tajikistan and Pakistan, a high valley walled by glaciated peaks of the Pamir and Hindu Kush. Created as a buffer between empires.
features.look_for: Long narrow valley between ice peaks

features.name: Komodo Islands
features.description: Dry, golden-brown hilly islands with turquoise bays between Sumbawa and Flores, the only home of the Komodo dragon. Padar island's three-bay viewpoint is iconic.
features.look_for: Brown-golden islands with turquoise bays

features.name: Wakatobi
features.description: A chain of islands and huge atoll-like reefs southeast of Sulawesi, one of the richest coral reef areas on Earth. The Kaledupa reef is one of the world's longest barrier reefs.
features.look_for: Turquoise reef shapes in deep blue sea

features.name: Wuliangsuhai Lake
features.description: A reed-choked lake in the Hetao plain beside the Yellow River, fed by irrigation runoff, standing out against the Ulan Buh desert. One of the largest wetlands on the Yellow River.
features.look_for: Green reedy lake by irrigated plain

features.name: Dune du Pilat
features.description: Europe's tallest sand dune (~105 m), a 3 km wedge of pale sand between the Arcachon Bay entrance and dark pine forest.
features.look_for: Bright sand strip between ocean and dark forest

features.name: Carrara marble quarries
features.description: Brilliant white marble scars all over the Apuan Alps, quarried since Roman times - the source of Michelangelo's David.
features.look_for: Bright white patches on green mountains

features.name: Mount Edgecumbe
features.description: A symmetrical dormant volcano near Sitka, famous for a 1974 April Fools prank in which tires were burned in its crater to fake an eruption.
features.look_for: Symmetrical cone with summit crater on Kruzof Island

features.name: Carrizozo Malpais
features.description: A 75 km lava flow from about 5,000 years ago, one of the youngest in the continental US, crossing the Tularosa Basin north of White Sands.
features.look_for: Long black tongue of lava across a pale desert valley

verified.note: black lava tongue in pale valley

features.name: Bermuda Platform
features.description: The northernmost coral reef system in the Atlantic, a pseudo-atoll capping an extinct volcano, with the islands curled along its southeast edge.
features.look_for: Fishhook of islands on the rim of a large turquoise reef platform

features.name: Ribbon Reefs
features.description: A chain of narrow, ribbon-like reefs running along the edge of the continental shelf off Cooktown for about 100 km. Beyond them the seafloor plunges to over 1,000 m.
features.look_for: Thin line of narrow reefs at the shelf edge

features.name: Raivavae
features.description: A small volcanic island in the Austral Islands, set in a broad turquoise lagoon ringed by sandy motu. It is often called one of the most beautiful islands in the Pacific.
features.look_for: Green island in a wide turquoise lagoon

features.name: Nikumaroro
features.description: An uninhabited atoll in the Phoenix Islands with a long narrow lagoon. It is the leading hypothesis for where Amelia Earhart made her final landing in 1937.
features.look_for: Elongated atoll with turquoise lagoon

features.name: Beardmore Glacier
features.description: One of the largest valley glaciers in the world, a 200 km ice river that Shackleton and Scott used as a highway to the polar plateau.
features.look_for: Wide striped glacier through mountains

features.name: Kharga Oasis
features.description: A long depression in Egypt's Western Desert lined by a cliff, with oasis farms dotted along its floor and dune lines streaming across it from the north.
features.look_for: Scarp-lined depression with dune streaks

features.name: Matobo Hills
features.description: A rumpled patch of bare granite domes, kopjes and balancing boulders in SW Zimbabwe, standing out as pale rock among the bush. Cecil Rhodes is buried on one of the domes.
features.look_for: Granite domes

features.name: Chilika Lake
features.description: Asia's largest brackish lagoon, a pear-shaped body behind a long sandbar on the Bay of Bengal. Irrawaddy dolphins and over a million wintering birds live here.
features.look_for: Pear-shaped lagoon behind a thin barrier beach

features.name: Mount Popa
features.description: An extinct volcano with a collapsed crater rising from the dry plains near Bagan, its forested slopes a green island; the nearby Taung Kalat pinnacle holds a monastery.
features.look_for: Forested volcano with horseshoe crater in dry plain

features.name: Sabah Oil Palm Plantations
features.description: Endless contour-terraced oil palm estates replace Borneo's rainforest in eastern Sabah, with rectilinear road grids cut into hills. Malaysia is the world's second-largest palm oil producer.
features.look_for: Regular grid texture of plantations against wild forest

features.name: Holuhraun
features.description: A fresh 85 km² lava field from the 2014-15 Bárðarbunga fissure eruption, a jet-black lobe spreading north of Vatnajökull.
features.look_for: Fresh black lava flow over grey sands

verified.note: dark lava field north of the ice

features.name: Monument Valley
features.description: Sandstone buttes up to 300 m tall stand on a flat red plain, the last remnants of an eroded plateau. A John Ford western staple.
features.look_for: Isolated red buttes and mesas casting long shadows on sandy plain

features.name: Gatún Lake & Panama Canal
features.description: Created in 1913 to carry ships across Panama, it was then the largest artificial lake in the world; Barro Colorado Island in it is a famous research station.
features.look_for: Island-studded reservoir crossing the isthmus

features.name: Atakor Volcanic Field
features.description: The volcanic heart of the Hoggar, a dark field of cones, plugs and lava sheets around Mount Tahat, Algeria's highest point (2,908 m).
features.look_for: Dark speckled volcanic field

features.name: Deosai Plains
features.description: One of the highest plateaus in the world (avg. 4,114 m), a green alpine plain amid snowy peaks, home to Himalayan brown bears. Snow-covered for most of the year.
features.look_for: Smooth high plain amid rugged mountains

features.name: Nagarjuna Sagar Reservoir
features.description: A long branching reservoir in the Krishna River gorge; its masonry dam is one of the largest in the world. Buddhist ruins were moved to an island in it.
features.look_for: Branching reservoir in rocky hills

features.name: Phang Nga Bay
features.description: A shallow bay studded with dozens of sheer limestone karst islands and lined with mangroves, made famous by 'The Man with the Golden Gun'. Many islands hide inner lagoons (hongs).
features.look_for: Bay full of small steep green islets

features.name: Laguna de Fuente de Piedra
features.description: Andalusia's largest natural lake, a white salt flat in summer that hosts western Europe's biggest flamingo colony.
features.look_for: White-pale oval lake in olive country

features.name: Coorong
features.description: A lagoon over 100 km long and as little as 2 km wide, separated from the Southern Ocean by the narrow Younghusband Peninsula dunes. It is where the Murray reaches the sea.
features.look_for: Long thin lagoon parallel to the coast

features.name: Rabaul caldera
features.description: A drowned caldera forming Simpson Harbour on New Britain, ringed by active cones. Tavurvur's 1994 eruption buried the old town of Rabaul in ash.
features.look_for: Round harbour with volcanic cones

features.name: Misool karst islands
features.description: A large island surrounded by hundreds of jungle-covered limestone islets and lagoons in southern Raja Ampat, part of the world's richest coral reef area.
features.look_for: Island fringed with many small karst islets

features.name: Easter Island
features.description: A triangle of grassy volcanic land in the open Pacific, with a volcano at each corner. It is famous for its moai statues and is the most remote inhabited island on Earth.
features.look_for: Triangular green-brown island

features.name: Clipperton Island
features.description: A remote ring-shaped atoll in the eastern Pacific with a completely enclosed lagoon of stagnant water. Its tragic WWI-era story of abandoned settlers inspired books and films.
features.look_for: Closed ring atoll

features.name: Pine Island Glacier
features.description: The fastest-melting glacier in Antarctica, whose floating tongue repeatedly cracks off city-sized icebergs into the Amundsen Sea.
features.look_for: Crevassed ice shelf with rifts

features.name: Pangong Tso
features.description: A very long, narrow lake at 4,225 m strung across the India-China border, shifting from turquoise to deep blue along its length. It freezes over completely in winter despite being saline.
features.look_for: Long thin blue lake in barren mountains

features.name: Nanga Parbat
features.description: The western anchor of the Himalaya (8,126 m) with the Rupal Face, the highest mountain wall on Earth at 4,600 m. It rises 7,000 m above the Indus in just 25 km.
features.look_for: Massive isolated snow massif above a desert valley

features.name: Jakarta
features.description: One of the world's largest metropolitan areas, a vast grey sprawl on the coast of Java, sinking so fast that Indonesia is moving its capital to Borneo. Fish ponds and new seawalls line its bay.
features.look_for: Huge grey sprawl on a flat coast

features.name: Dungeness
features.description: One of the world's largest shingle forelands, a triangular cuspate point of bare gravel ridges with a nuclear power station on its tip.
features.look_for: Pointed triangular foreland of pale shingle

features.name: Mount Edziza
features.description: A large volcanic complex whose plateau is dotted with dozens of young cinder cones and colorful lava flows such as the Spectrum Range.
features.look_for: Ice-capped volcano with red, yellow and black cinder cones on its flanks

features.name: San Luis Valley Pivots
features.description: A high-desert valley at 2,300 m irrigated by thousands of center pivots, making polka-dots of potato and barley fields.
features.look_for: Grid of green center-pivot circles in a high mountain valley

features.name: Colorado River Delta
features.description: Once a lush delta, it now rarely gets river water; huge tides (up to 7 m) in the Gulf of California etch tree-like channels into the barren mud.
features.look_for: Branching fractal tidal channels on bare mud flats

features.name: Kolyma Reservoir
features.description: A long, serpentine flooded valley of the upper Kolyma in the stark mountains of Magadan Oblast. Built in permafrost, which made it a notable engineering feat.
features.look_for: Thin twisting dark water in bare mountains

features.name: Salinas Grandes (Córdoba)
features.description: A vast 6,000 km² salt basin in the lowlands of Córdoba and Catamarca, bright white streaks against the dry Chaco scrub.
features.look_for: Bright white irregular basin in tan scrub

features.name: Paraná Delta
features.description: A huge wetland delta of channels and islands pushing into the Río de la Plata; its mud front advances up to 70 m a year toward Buenos Aires.
features.look_for: Green-brown delta with brown plume

features.name: Waterberg Plateau
features.description: A long sandstone plateau with sheer red cliffs rising from the bush, a dark tablet on the savanna that became a refuge for rare antelope and rhino.
features.look_for: Plateau with cliffs

features.name: Pilanesberg
features.description: One of the world's largest alkaline ring complexes, a nearly circular 27 km bullseye of concentric hills rising from the Bushveld plains, now a game reserve.
features.look_for: Circular ring complex

features.name: Wadi As-Sirhan Center Pivots
features.description: Thousands of center-pivot circles in the desert of northern Saudi Arabia, irrigated with fossil groundwater. They look like a sheet of polka dots.
features.look_for: Polka-dot pivot circles

features.name: Band-e Amir
features.description: A chain of six deep-blue lakes dammed by natural travertine walls in the arid Hindu Kush, unlike anything around them. Afghanistan's first national park.
features.look_for: Chain of intensely blue lakes in barren hills

features.name: Flevoland
features.description: The world's largest artificial island, polders pumped dry in the 1950s-60s and laid out in a rigid grid of long rectangular fields.
features.look_for: Huge reclaimed island of perfectly rectangular fields

features.name: Bardenas Reales
features.description: A semi-desert of clay badlands, mesas and gullies in Navarre, with a perfectly rectangular military bombing range in its middle.
features.look_for: Pale eroded badlands with a rectangular range

features.name: Outer Banks
features.description: A 320 km arc of barrier islands enclosing Pamlico Sound, the second largest estuary in the US; the Wright brothers first flew at Kitty Hawk here.
features.look_for: Long hair-thin barrier islands bowing out to Cape Hatteras

features.name: Andros Island
features.description: The largest island of the Bahamas, riddled with blue holes; its west coast is a vast wilderness of tidal mud flats and mangroves.
features.look_for: Large flat island with tidal creeks and blue holes, west side all mud flats

features.name: Erdenet Mine
features.description: A big copper-molybdenum open pit beside the city of Erdenet, with a huge pale tailings pond in the green northern Mongolian hills.
features.look_for: White tailings pond and grey pit by a city

verified.note: recentered between pit and tailings pond

features.name: Salar del Hombre Muerto
features.description: A "dead man's" salt flat in the Catamarca Puna with lithium evaporation ponds forming bright blocks along its western edge.
features.look_for: White salar with geometric ponds

features.name: Taylor Valley
features.description: A dry valley holding ice-covered lakes, with Taylor Glacier spilling into its head; its iron-rich brine leaks out as the blood-red Blood Falls.
features.look_for: Brown valley with frozen lakes

verified.note: valley with frozen lakes and glacier

features.name: Faiyum Oasis
features.description: A green bowl of farmland in the desert west of the Nile, with the dark salt lake Qarun along its northern edge. Fed by a canal from the Nile since pharaonic times.
features.look_for: Green bowl with a dark lake

features.name: Mount Fuji
features.description: Japan's iconic symmetrical stratovolcano (3,776 m), with a summit crater and radiating snow gullies, ringed by the Fuji Five Lakes on its north side. It last erupted in 1707.
features.look_for: Perfect cone with white radial snow streaks

features.name: Ariake Sea
features.description: A shallow bay in Kyushu with Japan's largest tides (up to 6 m), with huge mudflats and dense grids of nori seaweed farms. The Isahaya Bay dyke cut off part of it in 1997.
features.look_for: Brown bay with grid patterns of seaweed farms

features.name: Chitwan National Park
features.description: A sharply bounded block of dark sal forest and grassland in the Terai lowlands, surrounded by farmland. Home to rhinos and Bengal tigers.
features.look_for: Dark forest block with sharp edge against fields

features.name: Kelimutu
features.description: A volcano on Flores with three summit crater lakes of different colors (turquoise, green, black) that change hue over the years. Locals believe souls rest in them.
features.look_for: Three differently colored small crater lakes

verified.note: three colored lakes clear at z14; tiny

features.name: Mahakam Delta
features.description: A beautiful fan-shaped delta on Borneo's east coast, its fingers of land almost entirely converted to shrimp ponds that make a fine patchwork. Gas fields lie beneath.
features.look_for: Fan-shaped delta of fingers and pond patchwork

features.name: Peary Land
features.description: Earth's northernmost land: a largely ice-free polar desert of bare brown plateaus and valleys, fronted by permanent sea ice.
features.look_for: Bare brown land at the top of the world

features.name: Doñana marshes
features.description: Europe's great wetland at the Guadalquivir mouth: marshes, mobile dunes and a long beach, with the rice-field grid of Isla Mayor to the north.
features.look_for: Flat marsh behind coastal dunes

features.name: Soufrière Hills
features.description: Eruptions since 1995 buried the capital Plymouth and covered southern Montserrat in grey pyroclastic deposits, extending the coastline.
features.look_for: Grey ash-buried southern half of a green island

features.name: Manam
features.description: An almost perfectly round volcanic island, 10 km across, with radiating erosion gullies, one of PNG's most active volcanoes. Eruptions forced the evacuation of its whole population in 2004.
features.look_for: Round island with radial ridges

features.name: Ouvéa
features.description: A crescent-shaped atoll in the Loyalty Islands with a 25 km white beach and a vast turquoise lagoon dotted with islands. It is called "the island closest to paradise".
features.look_for: Crescent atoll with turquoise lagoon

features.name: Atafu
features.description: The smallest and northernmost atoll of Tokelau, a sharp triangle of white reef enclosing a lagoon patterned with dark coral pinnacles. Its whole population lives on a single islet.
features.look_for: Triangular reef ring with mottled lagoon

features.name: Ailinglaplap Atoll
features.description: A large triangular Marshallese atoll with more than 50 islets around a broad deep lagoon. It is the homeland of several chiefly lineages of the Ralik chain.
features.look_for: Triangular atoll ring

features.name: Sierra de Famatina
features.description: A high range (6,097 m) rising alone above La Rioja's deserts, snow-dusted and streaked with the colors of old copper and gold workings.
features.look_for: Snow-tipped range in desert

features.name: Tadrart Acacus
features.description: A dark, deeply carved sandstone range in SW Libya, its canyons partially filled by orange dunes. UNESCO-listed for thousands of rock paintings.
features.look_for: Dark ridge buried by orange dunes

features.name: Namib Sand Sea
features.description: A sea of brick-red dunes along Namibia's Atlantic coast, among the tallest in the world at up to 300 m. The colour comes from iron oxide coating the quartz grains.
features.look_for: Red dune sea by the ocean

features.name: Nanda Devi
features.description: India's second-highest peak (7,816 m), surrounded by a ring of peaks forming the Nanda Devi Sanctuary, a natural fortress. A lost CIA nuclear spy device is said to lie on its slopes.
features.look_for: Twin peak inside a ring of ridges

features.name: Jotunheimen
features.description: Norway's highest mountains (Galdhøpiggen 2,469 m), a dark crowd of peaks with glaciers and long finger lakes like Gjende.
features.look_for: Dense dark peaks with glaciers and turquoise lakes

features.name: Archipelago Sea
features.description: The world's largest archipelago by number of islands: some 40,000 islands and skerries between Turku and Åland.
features.look_for: Extremely dense scatter of islands

features.name: Severn Estuary
features.description: Funnel-shaped estuary with the world's second-largest tidal range (15 m), revealing vast muddy sandbanks at low tide.
features.look_for: Funnel estuary with brown water and sandbanks

features.name: Inglefield Fjord
features.description: A wide fjord near Qaanaaq lined by a row of outlet glaciers, often frozen white for most of the year.
features.look_for: Wide fjord fed by many glaciers

features.name: Mount Shasta
features.description: A 4,322 m stratovolcano standing alone above the surrounding plains, with glaciers on its upper slopes and a satellite cone, Shastina.
features.look_for: Isolated snow-capped cone towering over brown and green lowland

features.name: Carlin Trend Gold Mines
features.description: The Carlin Trend is the most prolific gold district in the Western Hemisphere, with gold too fine to see with a microscope.
features.look_for: Big terraced pits and waste dumps in sagebrush hills

features.name: Lake Alexandrina
features.description: A broad shallow freshwater lake at the mouth of the Murray River, separated from the sea by barrages. It is home to the Ngarrindjeri people.
features.look_for: Large milky-green lake near the coast

features.name: Menindee Lakes
features.description: A cluster of large round lakes beside the Darling River, now dammed as a water storage. Their pastel greens and browns stand out against red outback soils.
features.look_for: Round green lakes beside a winding river

features.name: Elizabeth Reef
features.description: One of the world's southernmost coral atolls, an oval reef enclosing a turquoise lagoon in the Tasman Sea. It is almost entirely submerged at high tide.
features.look_for: Oval turquoise atoll in the Tasman Sea

features.name: Mili Atoll
